teile.einleitung: Calming signals are soothing body signals with which dogs avoid arguments and calm themselves or others. They include, for example, yawning, looking away or sitting down slowly. Anyone who knows these signs understands much better how a dog is feeling at that moment.
wichtigste: In German, calming signals are called roughly “Beruhigungssignale” or “Beschwichtigungssignale”.
Dogs use them to avoid conflicts.
Typical signals are yawning, turning the head away, licking the nose and sniffing the ground.
The term was made known by the Norwegian dog trainer Turid Rugaas.
Dogs show such signals to other dogs and also to people.
A yawning dog is therefore not always tired, but sometimes tense.
Anyone who recognises calming signals can spare dogs stress and avoid bites.

abschnitte.text: **Calming signals** are small gestures of body language with which a dog shows: “I do not want a fight.” Dogs descend from the wolf and live in groups, so it is important for them to settle conflicts peacefully. With such signals they can defuse a tense situation. In doing so they also calm themselves when they are unsure or stressed.

A common signal is **yawning** even though the dog is not tired at all. Many dogs briefly lick their nose, turn the head to the side or blink. Others suddenly sniff the ground, walk in a curve round a strange dog or move conspicuously slowly. Sitting down, lying down or an invitation to play with the front of the body lowered can also have a calming effect.

The Norwegian dog trainer **Turid Rugaas** watched the behaviour of many dogs for years. She described about 30 such signals and in the 1990s published a book about them that was translated into many languages. Since then the English term has also been widespread in German. Experts in animal behaviour still discuss which signals are really always meant to be calming.

If a dog yawns, looks away or licks its nose while you are stroking it, it may feel uncomfortable. Then it is better to give it **space** and leave it in peace. You should not stare a strange dog in the eyes, lean over it or hug it. It is best always to ask the owner before touching a dog.

People too can use some of these signals to calm an anxious dog. For example you can stand slightly sideways, look away or speak slowly and calmly. For the dog this is less **threatening** than walking straight up with eye contact. In dog schools in Switzerland, owners often learn to read their dog's body language better.

begriffe.erklaerung: Messages that are conveyed without words through posture, movement and face.
Soothing someone so that no argument arises.
An argument or a tense situation between two or more living things.
A feeling of tension when something is too much, too close or frightening.

gewusst: Dogs show some calming signals so quickly that people often do not notice them at all.
Wolves also use similar signals to avoid arguments in the pack.
Many bite accidents with children happen because warning signals from the dog were overlooked.

teile.einleitung: The Altiplano is a huge high plateau in the Andes in South America. On average it lies at about 3,700 metres, so higher than most Swiss mountain peaks. Llamas, alpacas and flamingos live here, and here lie the famous Lake Titicaca and the largest salt desert in the world.
wichtigste: The Altiplano is a high plateau in the Andes.
It lies mainly in Bolivia and Peru, with small parts in Chile and Argentina.
The average height is about 3,700 metres above sea level.
Many alpacas, llamas and vicuñas live on the Altiplano.
Lake Titicaca lies on the northern edge of the Altiplano.
The Salar de Uyuni is the largest salt flat on Earth.
Peoples such as the Aymara and Quechua have lived here for centuries.

abschnitte.text: The name **Altiplano** is Spanish and means “high plain”. It lies between two mountain chains of the **Andes**, the Western Cordillera and the Eastern Cordillera. The plateau is about 1,000 kilometres long and extends over Peru, Bolivia, Chile and Argentina. After the Tibetan Plateau, the Altiplano is one of the largest high plateaus in the world. Most of it lies in Bolivia.

On the Altiplano the air is thin, dry and cold. By day the sun shines strongly, and at night temperatures often fall below zero degrees. Almost no trees grow, but mainly hard grasses and cushion plants, called **puna**. In the south it is very dry, and there are salt lakes and deserts. At the edge, volcanoes rise to over 6,000 metres in height.

abschnitte.titel: Lake Titicaca and Salar de Uyuni
abschnitte.text: In the north lies **Lake Titicaca** at about 3,810 metres, shared between Peru and Bolivia. It is considered the highest navigable lake in the world and is about 15 times as large as Lake Constance. In the south lies the **Salar de Uyuni**, a salt flat of over 10,000 square kilometres. After rain the sky is reflected in it as in a giant mirror. Under the salt lie large amounts of lithium, which is used for batteries.

The Altiplano is the home of the **alpacas** and **llamas**, which have been kept here for thousands of years. Wild here live the dainty **vicuñas**, whose wool is among the finest in the world. In the salt lakes stand flamingos, for example the Andean flamingo and the James’s flamingo. Between rocks scurry viscachas, which are rodents that look like hares with a long tail. In the sky the Andean condor sometimes circles.

On the Altiplano live mainly people of the **Aymara** and **Quechua** peoples. They grow potatoes, quinoa and barley and keep llamas and alpacas. The potato originally comes from this region of the Andes. On the edge of the Altiplano lie the cities of La Paz and El Alto in Bolivia. Even before the Incas, there was the high culture of Tiwanaku here, near Lake Titicaca.

begriffe.erklaerung: A large, fairly flat landscape that lies high above the sea.
A flat hollow in which a lake has evaporated and left behind a thick layer of salt.
Headache and nausea that can arise when you get to a great height too quickly, because the air has little oxygen.
A wild, slender camel of the Andes with very fine wool.

gewusst: On the Altiplano, water boils at only about 87 degrees, because the air pressure is so low.
The people on Lake Titicaca build floating islands from reeds, the Uros Islands.
The Salar de Uyuni is so flat that it is used to calibrate satellites.

teile.einleitung: Brood parasitism is what it is called when an animal has its eggs incubated by others and its young raised by foreign parents. The best-known example is the cuckoo, which secretly lays its eggs in the nests of small songbirds. For the host parents this is a hard trick, because in the end they feed a strange chick.
wichtigste: Brood parasitism means that a bird has its eggs incubated by other birds.
The cuckoo is the best-known brood parasite in Europe.
The birds that incubate the foreign egg are called host birds.
Cuckoo eggs often look very similar to the eggs of the host birds.
The cuckoo chick throws the other eggs or chicks out of the nest.
Some insects and even fish also practise brood parasitism.
Many host birds have developed defence tricks.

abschnitte.text: A **parasite** is a living thing that lives at the expense of another. In brood parasitism an animal exploits the brood care of another species or another animal. It builds no nest of its own, does not incubate and does not feed its young itself. In this way it saves a great deal of energy and can lay more eggs.

The female **cuckoo** watches the nests of songbirds such as reed warblers, black redstarts or pied wagtails. At a favourable moment she lays an egg in it within seconds and often takes one of the host's eggs away with her. The cuckoo chick usually hatches earlier than the others and pushes eggs and siblings out of the nest with its back. After that it is fed by the small host parents until it is much bigger than they are themselves.

Female cuckoos specialise in certain host species, and their eggs often have a similar colour to the host eggs. Many host birds nevertheless recognise foreign eggs and throw them out or abandon the nest. That is why both sides keep developing new adaptations, a so-called **arms race** of evolution. The cuckoo chick also begs so loudly that it sounds as if several chicks were in the nest.

It is not only cuckoos that are brood parasites, the American **brown-headed cowbird**, African whydahs and honeyguides belong here too. In ducks some females lay eggs in the nests of other ducks of the same species. Among insects there are cuckoo bumblebees and cuckoo bees that smuggle their eggs into foreign nests. In Lake Tanganyika in Africa there even lives a cuckoo catfish that mixes its eggs among the eggs of mouthbrooding cichlids.

In Switzerland the cuckoo is a **migratory bird** that returns from Africa in April. Its well-known call “cuckoo” comes from the male. In Switzerland there are fewer cuckoos than in the past, among other reasons because large insects such as hairy caterpillars have become rarer. Anyone who walks in the woods or at the woodland edge in spring can still often hear it, though.

begriffe.erklaerung: A living thing that lives at the expense of another.
A bird that incubates a foreign egg and raises the foreign chick.
Everything that parents do so that their young survive, for example incubating and feeding.
The slow change of living things over many generations.

gewusst: A female cuckoo can lay many eggs in different foreign nests in one season.
A young cuckoo can in the end weigh several times as much as its foster parents.
The cuckoo spends the winter in Africa south of the Sahara.

teile.einleitung: The bison is a mighty wild ox from North America and a relative of the African Cape buffalo. In the past millions of bison roamed across the prairies, then they were almost wiped out. Today the bison is the national mammal of the USA.
wichtigste: The American bison is the largest land animal in North America.
Like the Cape buffalo, it belongs to the bovid family and is related to it.
Bulls can weigh about 900 kg and more.
In the past many millions of bison probably lived on the prairies of North America.
In the 19th century the bison were almost wiped out.
For many Indigenous peoples of the prairie the bison was the most important basis of life.
In Yellowstone National Park bison have lived wild without a break since prehistoric times.

abschnitte.text: The **American bison** has a huge head, a high hump above the shoulders and short, curved horns. At the front it carries a long, shaggy mane, and at the back the fur is shorter. Bulls grow up to about two metres high and often weigh over 900 kg. Cows are clearly smaller. Despite their size, bison can run up to about 55 km/h.

The bison belongs to the family of **bovids**, which also includes domestic cattle, yaks, the European bison and the **Cape buffalo**. Its closest relative is the European bison, or wisent. It is more distantly related to the Cape buffalo, but both are large wild oxen that live in herds. In English the bison is often called “buffalo”, although it is not a true buffalo. A distinction is made between the plains bison and the larger wood bison.

Bison live in herds on grassland and in open woods. They eat mainly grasses and are **ruminants**. In winter they push the snow aside with their heads to get at the grass. They like to roll in the dust to get rid of insects, and such places are called wallows. A calf is born in spring and is reddish brown at first.

Before the Europeans arrived, probably 30 million or more bison lived in North America. In the 19th century they were shot in huge numbers, often only for their hides and tongues. The aim was also to take away the basis of life from the **Indigenous peoples** of the prairie. Around 1890 only a few hundred wild bison were left. Some ranchers and conservationists saved the last animals.

Today there are again several hundred thousand bison, most of them, however, on farms. Wild herds are found mainly in protected areas such as **Yellowstone National Park** in the USA and Wood Buffalo National Park in Canada. In 2016 the bison was declared the national mammal of the USA. For many Indigenous communities it is still a sacred animal today, and they are bringing it back onto their land.

begriffe.erklaerung: A family of even-toed ungulates with horns that stay for life, such as cattle, sheep and goats.
Wide grassland in North America.
Plant eaters that bring their food back up and chew it again.

gewusst: Despite their weight, bison can jump almost two metres high and swim well.
In Yellowstone National Park visitors are injured every year because they get too close to bison.

teile.einleitung: The queen bee is the mother of all the bees in a bee colony. She is the only bee in the hive that lays eggs, often thousands in a single day. Despite her name she does not rule, but provides the next generation.
wichtigste: In every bee colony there is normally only one queen.
The queen lays all the eggs in the beehive.
To be able to lay eggs she needs a nuptial flight with drones.
A queen can live for several years, workers in summer only a few weeks.
She is bigger and has a longer abdomen than the workers.
A queen arises when a larva is fed only on royal jelly.
With scent substances the queen holds the colony together.

abschnitte.text: The **queen** is clearly longer than a worker, and above all her abdomen is long and slim. In it lie the ovaries, in which the eggs form. Her wings look short by comparison. She has a sting without barbs, which she uses almost only in fights against other queens. Beekeepers often mark the queen with a coloured dot so that they can find her in the crowd.

A queen develops from a quite ordinary fertilised egg. What matters is the food: the larva lies in a large, peg-shaped **queen cell** and gets only **royal jelly**, a special food secretion. This makes her a queen instead of a worker. After only about 16 days she hatches. If there are several young queens, they fight until only one is left.

A few days after hatching the young queen flies out on her **nuptial flight**. In the air she mates with several drones, the male bees. She stores the sperm in a small container in her body. This supply lasts for her whole life. After that she leaves the hive only when the colony swarms.

In spring and summer a queen lays up to about 2,000 eggs a day. She can decide herself whether an egg is fertilised. From fertilised eggs females arise, that is workers or new queens. From unfertilised eggs drones hatch. The workers feed and clean the queen constantly, because she herself does not look after the brood.

The queen gives off a special scent substance, a **pheromone**. By it all the bees notice that their queen is there and healthy. If this scent is missing, the workers quickly raise a new queen. If the colony grows too large, the old queen leaves the hive in spring with some of the bees, as a **bee swarm**. A queen can live for several years, usually about three to five.

begriffe.erklaerung: A special food secretion that young workers make and with which queen larvae are fed.
A large comb cell hanging downwards in which a queen grows up.
A male honey bee.
A scent substance with which animals send each other messages.

gewusst: On one day a queen sometimes lays more eggs than she weighs herself.
An old German word for the queen bee is “Weisel”.
Beekeepers mark queens with a colour that reveals the year of birth.

teile.einleitung: A guide dog is a specially trained dog that leads blind or severely visually impaired people safely through everyday life. It indicates obstacles, stairs and kerbs. In this way its person can get about independently, go to work or do the shopping.
wichtigste: A guide dog leads and supports a visually impaired person in everyday life.
It goes round obstacles and stops at stairs and kerbs.
They are often Labrador retrievers, golden retrievers or shepherd dogs.
The training takes about one and a half to two years.
While working the dog wears a harness with a handle.
A working guide dog should not be stroked or distracted.

abschnitte.text: A guide dog is an **assistance dog** for people who cannot see or can hardly see. It walks on the left next to its person and leads them round obstacles. At stairs, kerbs and doors it stops and so indicates them. On command it finds, for example, a free seat, an entrance or a pedestrian crossing. The person gives the direction, and the dog makes sure the way is safe.

Suitable puppies first live for about a year with a **puppy-raising family**. There they get to know people, traffic, buses and trains. After that comes training of several months at a guide dog school. In Switzerland the best known is the school for guide dogs in **Allschwil** in the canton of Basel-Landschaft. At the end the dog and the new handler practise together until they are a well-rehearsed team.

A guide dog sometimes has to refuse a command. If its person wants to cross the road although a car is coming, the dog stops. This is called **intelligent disobedience**. It also watches for obstacles at head height, such as branches or signs that the person would not feel with the cane. The colour of the traffic light, though, is decided by the person, because dogs do not see red and green well.

**Labrador retrievers** and golden retrievers are especially often trained. German shepherds and crosses of these breeds are also suitable. A good guide dog is calm, friendly, attentive and not easily distracted. After about eight to ten working years guide dogs retire and often go on living with their family or a host family.

The first school for guide dogs was set up in 1916 in Germany. It trained dogs for soldiers who had gone blind in the **First World War**. Later the idea spread in Europe and America. The Swiss school in Allschwil was founded in 1972.

A guide dog in its **harness** is at work and has to concentrate. You should therefore not stroke it, feed it or call it. Anyone who wants to help is best to speak to the person and ask whether help is wanted. Guide dogs may usually accompany their handlers into shops, restaurants and public transport as well.

begriffe.erklaerung: A specially trained dog that helps people with a disability.
A strap with a firm handle that the person holds onto.
A family that brings up a young dog before its training.
When a person sees badly or not at all.

gewusst: A guide dog always walks on the left of its person.
Not every puppy becomes a guide dog, some are too playful or timid and get a different job.
Guide dogs learn dozens of voice commands, for example for door, stairs or seat.

teile.einleitung: Aphids are tiny insects that sit on plants and suck their sweet sap. In spring they often appear suddenly in huge numbers, for example on roses or beans. For gardeners they are a nuisance, but for many other animals they are important food.
wichtigste: Aphids are small insects that suck plant sap.
They belong to the insect order of the true bugs (Hemiptera).
Aphids can be green, black, yellow or reddish.
There are winged and wingless adult aphids.
Ants protect aphids and collect their sweet honeydew.
Aphids can transmit plant viruses.
Ladybirds, lacewings and tits eat many aphids.

abschnitte.text: Aphids are usually only 1 to 4 millimetres in size and have a soft, roundish body. Their colour can be **green**, black, yellow or reddish, depending on the species. On the abdomen many species carry two small tubes, the **siphunculi**. From them they give off defensive substances when an enemy attacks. With their antennae they smell and feel to find suitable plants.

Aphids belong to the **true bugs**, which have a piercing beak. With it they pierce the vessels of the plant and suck the sugar-rich sap. Because the sap contains a lot of sugar but little protein, they have to drink a great deal of it. The surplus sugar they excrete again as sticky **honeydew**. That is why leaves and cars under infested trees sometimes gleam stickily.

In spring and summer many female aphids do not need a male to have young. This kind of reproduction is called **parthenogenesis**. The females even give birth to live young, which can themselves have young after only about a week. The larvae moult about four times before they are adult. If it gets crowded on a plant, winged animals appear that fly to new plants.

Aphids appear especially strongly in spring and early summer. Then it gets warm, and the young shoots are full of sap. In autumn males and females appear and mate. Many species survive the winter as **eggs** on plants, for example in cracks in the bark. The next spring new aphids hatch from them.

**Ants** love the sweet honeydew and stroke the aphids with their antennae so that they give it off. In return the ants defend their aphids against enemies, almost like shepherds their flock. The enemies include **ladybirds** and their larvae, lacewing larvae, hoverfly larvae and small parasitic wasps. Birds such as tits also like to eat aphids in the garden.

Aphids weaken plants because they draw sap from them, and can transmit dangerous **plant viruses**. In agriculture they can therefore do great damage. On house plants, spraying with water or a mild soapy solution often helps. In the garden it is good to encourage beneficial animals such as ladybirds instead of spraying poison. From honeydew, by the way, bees collect the dark forest honey.

begriffe.erklaerung: A sweet, sticky liquid that aphids excrete.
Two tubes on the abdomen from which defensive substances emerge.
Reproduction without a male, by the female alone.
An animal that eats pests and so helps people.

gewusst: A single ladybird larva can eat several hundred aphids in its life.
Some aphids are born with grandchildren already in their belly, because the next generation is already growing in the unborn young.
The dark forest honey comes to a large extent from the honeydew of aphids.

teile.einleitung: The pine marten is an agile predator from the marten family that lives in large forests. It climbs so skilfully that it can even hunt squirrels. It differs from its relative, the stone marten, by a yellowish patch on the throat.
wichtigste: The pine marten lives mainly in larger, unbroken forests.
Its yellowish throat patch is usually undivided, while in the stone marten it is white and forked.
It has hairy soles on its feet, the stone marten bare ones.
It climbs very skilfully and can jump from branch to branch.
It is active mainly at night and at dusk.
In it there is delayed implantation, which is why the gestation period is very long.
In Switzerland it occurs in forests throughout the country.

abschnitte.text: The pine marten has a slim body about 45 to 55 centimetres long and a bushy tail of around 25 centimetres. It weighs about one to one and a half kilograms. Its fur is chestnut brown, and on the throat it has a yellowish to orange **throat patch**, which is usually undivided. In the **stone marten** this patch is white and reaches forked down to the forelegs. The soles of the pine marten's feet are densely haired in winter.

The pine marten likes best to live in larger, unbroken **forests** with old trees. It occurs in almost all of Europe, in Switzerland up to the tree line in the Alps. It sleeps in tree holes, in old birds' nests or in squirrels' nests, called dreys. It tends to avoid people. The stone marten, by contrast, often lives near settlements and even sleeps in attics.

The pine marten is an **omnivore** with a preference for meat. It eats mice, birds, eggs, insects and in autumn also berries and fruit. Because it climbs very skilfully and can jump from branch to branch, it even catches squirrels. It hunts mainly at dusk and at night. In one night it often covers several kilometres.

Pine martens mate in high summer, usually in July or August. After that there is **delayed implantation**: the embryo waits for months before it implants in the womb. That is why the young are only born the following spring, usually in March or April. A litter consists of about two to five young. They are blind at first and are nursed for several weeks.

In the past the pine marten was hunted heavily for its valuable fur and was also called the **noble marten**. In some areas it became rare as a result. Today it is not threatened in Switzerland, but may only be hunted at certain times. Old forests with tree holes are important for it. It helps to keep the number of mice in the forest in balance.

begriffe.erklaerung: A family of slim predators with short legs that also includes the badger and the weasel.
A pale patch of fur on the throat.
A pause before the embryo implants in the womb.
The ball-shaped nest of a squirrel.

gewusst: Because of delayed implantation, the pine marten's gestation lasts eight to nine months, although the actual development takes only about a month.
Pine martens have a territory that can cover several square kilometres of forest.
Because pine martens hunt grey squirrels, they help the native squirrels in Britain.

teile.einleitung: The bear is one of the best-known heraldic animals, especially in Switzerland. A black bear decorates the coat of arms of the city and canton of Bern, but also the coats of arms of the two Appenzells. Cities such as Berlin and Madrid also have a bear on their coat of arms.
wichtigste: A heraldic animal is an animal that is shown on a coat of arms.
The bear decorates the coat of arms of the city and canton of Bern.
In the Bernese coat of arms a black bear walks on a golden diagonal band on a red field.
Appenzell Innerrhoden and Appenzell Ausserrhoden also have a black bear on their coat of arms.
The bear stands for strength, courage and readiness to defend.
Berlin and Madrid also have a bear on their coat of arms.

abschnitte.text: A **coat of arms** is an identifying sign on a shield that belongs to a family, city or country. Animals on coats of arms are called **heraldic animals**. Common ones are the lion, the eagle and the bear, because they are regarded as strong and mighty. The bear stands for strength, courage and readiness to defend.

The coat of arms of **Bern** shows on a red ground a golden diagonal band on which a black bear with a red tongue and red claws strides upwards. The city and canton of Bern use almost the same coat of arms. The bear can already be seen on old seals of the city from the 13th century. The people of Bern lovingly call their bear **Mutz**.

According to legend, Duke **Berchtold V of Zähringen** founded the city of Bern in 1191. He is said to have decided to name the city after the first animal killed on a hunt. This animal was a bear, and so the city is said to have got its name. Linguists, however, regard the origin of the name Bern as unexplained.

The cantons of **Appenzell Innerrhoden** and Appenzell Ausserrhoden also carry a black bear walking upright on a white ground. The coat of arms of Ausserrhoden also shows the letters V and R. The Appenzell bear comes from the coat of arms of the Abbey of St Gallen. It recalls the legend of Saint **Gallus**, to whom a bear is said to have brought wood for a fire.

**Berlin** also has a bear on its coat of arms, standing upright there. The coat of arms of Madrid shows a bear eating from a strawberry tree. Many municipalities in Switzerland and Germany also have bears on their coats of arms. In Bern, living bears even live in the Bear Park as emblems of the city.

begriffe.erklaerung: A sign on a shield that identifies a family, city or country.
An animal shown on a coat of arms.
A broad, slanting stripe across a coat of arms.
The Bernese German word for bear.

gewusst: With the Appenzell bear, the exact depiction of the bear once even led to a dispute with the city of St Gallen.
Since 1513 the city of Bern has kept living bears as heraldic animals, at first in various pits, today in the Bear Park on the Aare.

teile.einleitung: After the African elephant, the Asian elephant is the largest land animal on Earth. It lives in the forests and grasslands of South and South-East Asia. For thousands of years people have worked together with tamed Asian elephants.
wichtigste: The scientific name of the Asian elephant is Elephas maximus.
It lives in the wild in South and South-East Asia.
It has smaller ears than the African elephant and a forehead with two bulges.
A grown-up elephant eats over 100 kilograms of food a day.
A newborn calf weighs about 100 kilograms and first drinks its mother's milk.
Adult males mostly live alone or in small bachelor groups.
The species is highly endangered.

abschnitte.text: Asian elephants grow to about 3 metres tall, and the bulls weigh up to around 5 tonnes. Compared with African elephants they have smaller, rounded **ears**. Their forehead has two bulges, and the highest point of the body is the arched back. At the tip of the trunk they have only one finger-like projection, while African elephants have two. Only some of the bulls carry long **tusks**, and the cows have at most small tusklets.

The Asian elephant lives in the wild in South and South-East Asia, for example in India, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Myanmar, Malaysia and on Sumatra and Borneo. It feels at home in **forests** and grassland with water. Around 50,000 wild animals are still alive worldwide, most of them in India. Their habitat is often cut up into small pieces.

Elephants are pure **plant eaters**. A grown-up Asian elephant eats over 100 kilograms of grasses, leaves, bark, roots and fruit every day. It spends up to 18 hours a day busy eating. It also drinks a lot of water and likes to bathe. When swimming, it can use its trunk as a snorkel under water.

Females and young live in **herds** led by an experienced lead cow. Adult males mostly live alone or in small bachelor groups. An elephant cow is pregnant for about 22 months, longer than any other mammal. A newborn calf weighs about 100 kilograms and at first feeds on its mother's milk.

Tame Asian elephants used often to be used for carrying heavy **tree trunks** in the forest. They also played a role in wars and at religious festivals, for example at the Perahera festival in Sri Lanka. Today there are often conflicts when wild elephants raid fields. That is why in some countries people protect their fields with fences and ditches.

The Asian elephant is listed on the Red List as **endangered**. Threats are the loss of habitat, poaching for ivory and conflicts with people. In Switzerland you can see Asian elephants at Zurich Zoo, which opened the large **Kaeng Krachan Elephant Park** in 2014. The facility is named after a national park in Thailand.

begriffe.erklaerung: The long, flexible extension of an elephant's nose and upper lip.
Greatly lengthened incisor teeth made of ivory.
The oldest and most experienced elephant cow, who leads the herd.
A male elephant.

gewusst: An elephant's trunk has tens of thousands of muscles, but not a single bone.
Elephants can recognise themselves in a mirror, which only a few animals can do.
Asian elephants also communicate with very low sounds that people cannot hear.

teile.einleitung: Canis is the scientific name of a genus of predators from the dog family. It includes the wolf, the domestic dog, the coyote and the golden jackal. The Latin word “canis” simply means “dog”.
wichtigste: Canis is a genus in the dog family (Canidae).
The wolf, the domestic dog and the golden jackal belong to the genus Canis.
Jackals are therefore closely related to the wolf and the domestic dog.
The coyote of North America and the Ethiopian wolf belong here too.
The domestic dog descends from the wolf.
In Switzerland today wolves live again, and occasionally golden jackals.

abschnitte.text: In biology, living things are arranged in groups that keep getting larger: species, genus, family, order and so on. A **genus** brings together closely related species. Every species has a scientific name of two words, first the genus and then the species, for example Canis lupus for the wolf. This system was introduced by the Swedish naturalist Carl von Linné in the 18th century.

The best-known member is the **wolf** (Canis lupus), the largest wild member of the genus. The domestic dog is usually classified as a subspecies of the wolf (Canis lupus familiaris). In addition there are the North American **coyote**, the golden jackal, the African golden wolf and the rare Ethiopian wolf. Other species of jackal such as the black-backed jackal are today often placed in a genus of their own, but are also closely related.

Animals of the genus Canis have long legs, a long muzzle, upright ears and a bushy tail. They are good runners and can cover long distances. Their jaws have strong **canine teeth** and sharp carnassial teeth for cutting meat. Most live in family groups or packs and communicate with howling, barking and body language.

Many thousands of years ago people began to live together with wolves. From this the **domestic dog** gradually arose, the oldest domestic animal of humans. Through breeding, hundreds of breeds later arose, from the tiny Chihuahua to the large Great Dane. Because dogs and wolves are so closely related, they can even breed with each other.

The wolf was wiped out in Switzerland at the end of the 19th century and from 1995 migrated back in from Italy. Today several hundred wolves live in Switzerland again in many **packs**, above all in the Alps. The golden jackal was first recorded in Switzerland in 2011 and is slowly spreading from south-eastern Europe. The domestic dog is also a Canis and lives in many Swiss families.

begriffe.erklaerung: A group of closely related animal species.
A group of living things that can reproduce with each other and have healthy offspring.
A family group of wolves or other dog-like animals.
An especially sharp molar in predators that cuts meat like scissors.

gewusst: A Chihuahua and a wolf belong to the same species, although they look completely different.
The Ethiopian wolf lives only in the highlands of Ethiopia and is one of the rarest dog-like animals in the world.
The coyote has spread in North America into big cities such as Los Angeles and Chicago.

teile.einleitung: The woodlouse hunter is a spider that specialises in hunting woodlice. This means the woodlouse spiders of the genus Dysdera, above all the common woodlouse spider. With their huge fangs they pierce the hard armour of their prey.
wichtigste: Woodlouse spiders of the genus Dysdera specialise in hunting woodlice.
The best-known species is the common woodlouse spider, Dysdera crocata.
They have strikingly large fangs.
Their front body and legs are reddish brown, the abdomen is pale.
They have only six eyes instead of eight.
Woodlouse spiders do not build a catching web, but hunt at night on the ground.
They are harmless to people.

abschnitte.text: The **common woodlouse spider** grows to about 1 to 1.5 centimetres long, depending on its sex. The front body and legs are a strong reddish brown, the abdomen is pale grey to beige. Striking are the large, forward-pointing **chelicerae**, the fangs. Woodlouse spiders have six eyes that stand close together.

Woodlouse spiders live under stones, pieces of wood, bark and leaves, where it is damp. That is exactly where woodlice like to stay, too. The common woodlouse spider comes from the Mediterranean region, but has been carried by people to many parts of the world. It also occurs in Switzerland, often in gardens and sometimes in cellars.

**Woodlice** are small crustaceans with a hard, armoured back that many other predators avoid. Woodlouse spiders seize a woodlouse with their long fangs and stab one fang from below into the soft belly. The other fang often pierces the armour on the back. Besides woodlice, they also eat other small ground animals.

Woodlouse spiders are **nocturnal** and only go hunting in the dark. They do not build a catching web. They spend the day in a small, sack-like hiding place made of spider silk. The females also lay their eggs in such a silk sack and guard them.

Woodlouse spiders are not dangerous to people. If you pick them up, however, they can bite with their strong jaws. It feels like a needle prick and can itch or swell briefly. It is best to leave them alone, because they are useful residents of the garden.

begriffe.erklaerung: The fangs of a spider, with which it bites and injects venom.
A small crustacean with armour that lives on land in damp places.
An animal that is mainly on the move at night.
A group of very closely related species, here the genus Dysdera.

gewusst: The common woodlouse spider belongs to the family of six-eyed spiders.
Some species of the genus Dysdera have differently shaped jaws, depending on how they seize woodlice.
On the Canary Islands there are especially many different Dysdera species.

teile.einleitung: Bears are large, powerful predators with thick fur, a short tail and strong paws. The bear family includes, for example, the brown bear, the polar bear and the giant panda. In Switzerland the brown bear was wiped out, but single animals are now moving in again.
wichtigste: Bears form a family of their own within the carnivores, scientifically Ursidae.
The family includes, for example, the brown bear.
There are eight species of bear, including the polar bear, the American black bear and the giant panda.
Most bears eat both plants and meat.
Bears walk on the whole sole of the foot, they are plantigrade.
Many bears spend winter dormant in a den.
The last native bear of Switzerland was shot in 1904 in the Lower Engadine.

abschnitte.text: Bears form a family of carnivores with the scientific name **Ursidae**. Today there are eight species: the brown bear, the American black bear, the polar bear, the Asiatic black bear, the sun bear, the sloth bear, the spectacled bear and the **giant panda**. They live in Europe, Asia and America, and there are no bears in Africa or Australia. Together with large brown bears, the polar bear is the largest land predator.

Bears have a massive body, short legs, a short tail and small round ears. They walk on the whole sole of the foot and are therefore **plantigrade**, like us humans. On their paws they have long claws that they cannot draw in. Their sense of smell is excellent, much better than a dog's.

Although bears belong to the carnivores, most species eat very many plants. Brown bears eat grasses, berries, roots, insects, honey, but also fish and larger animals. The **polar bear** is almost a pure meat eater and hunts mainly seals. The giant panda, on the other hand, feeds almost only on **bamboo**.

Many bears spend the winter asleep in a den, which is called **winter dormancy**. They live on the fat reserves they ate in autumn. During this time the females give birth to their young. Newborn bear cubs are tiny, naked and blind and often weigh only a few hundred grams.

In the past brown bears lived in large parts of Switzerland. Through hunting they were wiped out, and the last native bear was shot in **1904** in the Lower Engadine. Since **2005**, single young bears have repeatedly migrated from the Italian Trentino into the Grisons. For encounters the rule is: keep your distance, retreat calmly and never leave food lying about.

Several species of bear are endangered, because their habitat is shrinking or they are hunted. The **polar bear** suffers because the sea ice in the Arctic is melting through global warming. In Asia, Asiatic black bears and sun bears are in part poached. Protected areas and laws are meant to help preserve the bears.

begriffe.erklaerung: The scientific name of the bear family.
An animal that walks on the whole sole of its foot.
A long winter sleep in which body temperature drops only a little.
An animal that eats plants and meat.

gewusst: Despite its weight, a brown bear can run faster than a human over a short distance.
The teddy bear was named after the American president Theodore Roosevelt, who was called Teddy.
Polar bears have black skin under their white fur.

teile.einleitung: The blue whale is the largest animal that has ever lived on Earth, bigger than any dinosaur. It can grow to over 30 metres long. Even so, it feeds on tiny crustaceans, the krill.
wichtigste: The blue whale is the largest and longest animal that has ever lived.
It can grow to over 30 metres long and weigh far more than 100 tonnes.
It eats tiny crustaceans called krill, not large fish.
Its heart is about as big as a small car.
Blue whales usually live alone or in small groups.
A calf drinks several hundred litres of milk a day.
The blue whale is highly endangered because it was hunted in huge numbers in the past.

abschnitte.text: The blue whale is a **baleen whale** and belongs to the rorquals. It usually grows 24 to 30 metres long, which is as long as two buses one behind the other. Its body is blue-grey with pale spots. On its back it has only a rather small **dorsal fin**. Its heart is about as big as a small car.

Although it is so big, the blue whale eats almost only **krill**, small crustaceans a few centimetres long. With its huge mouth it takes in many tonnes of water with krill. In doing so its throat with the grooves expands like a balloon. Then it presses the water out again through its **baleen plates**, and the krill stay caught. In one day a blue whale can eat several tonnes of krill.

The blue whale is a mammal and breathes with lungs. It has two **blowholes** on top of the head. Before it dives, it takes several deep breaths at the surface. When it breathes out, a fountain up to 9 metres high is produced, the blow. It usually dives for 10 to 20 minutes, sometimes longer.

Blue whales usually live alone or in small groups. About every two to three years a female has a **calf**, which at birth is already around 7 metres long. The calf drinks several hundred litres of fat-rich milk daily. As a result it grows very fast and puts on a lot of weight every day. Blue whales communicate with very deep, loud calls that can be heard over long distances.

Blue whales live in all the oceans of the world. In summer they feed in cold seas with a lot of krill, for example in the Antarctic. In winter many move to warmer waters to give birth to their young. In Switzerland you cannot see blue whales in the wild, because there is no sea. In natural history museums, though, you can marvel at skeletons and models of whales.

In the 20th century hundreds of thousands of blue whales were killed with harpoons, above all for their **whale oil**. They almost became extinct. Since 1966 hunting blue whales has been banned worldwide. Today the populations are slowly recovering, but the blue whale is still considered highly endangered. Dangers today are above all collisions with ships, noise and climate change.

begriffe.erklaerung: Plates of horn in the mouth that filter food out of the water like a sieve.
Small crustaceans that live in the sea in huge swarms.
A fountain of air and water vapour when a whale breathes out.
An animal that feeds its young with milk.

gewusst: The tongue of a blue whale can weigh as much as an elephant.
A blue whale calf puts on about 90 kilograms a day in its first months.
The calls of blue whales are among the loudest sounds that an animal can make.

teile.einleitung: The Braunvieh is a well-known Swiss breed of cow with grey-brown fur. It comes from central Switzerland and is one of the oldest breeds of cattle in the world. Today it is found as a dairy cow on all continents.
wichtigste: The Braunvieh is a well-known Swiss breed of cattle with brown fur.
It originally comes from central Switzerland, above all from the area around Schwyz.
Typical are a pale ring around the dark muzzle and pale horns with dark tips.
There is the original Braunvieh and the Brown Swiss bred for milk.
Braunvieh is robust and well suited to the Alps.
A lot of cheese is made from its milk.
Braunvieh is kept all over the world today.

abschnitte.text: Braunvieh cows have **grey-brown** to dark brown fur that is lighter or darker depending on the animal. The muzzle, called the Flotzmaul in German, is dark and surrounded by a pale ring. The horns are pale with dark tips, though the horns of many cows are removed. A cow usually weighs about 600 to 700 kilograms. Braunvieh is regarded as calm, undemanding and **robust**.

The Braunvieh comes from **central Switzerland**, above all from the area around Schwyz. That is why in the past it was also called Schwyz cattle. It was bred in the Alps over centuries and is adapted to steep pastures and a rough mountain climate. Later it spread throughout eastern Switzerland, the Grisons and Ticino. The Braunvieh is one of the oldest breeds of cattle there is.

From the 19th century Braunvieh animals were sold abroad, for example to Italy, Germany and in 1869 to the USA. In America a pure dairy breed was bred from it, the **Brown Swiss**. This was later also brought back to Switzerland. Today there is Braunvieh in very many countries of the world, from Mexico to India.

The **original Braunvieh** is a dual-purpose breed that supplies both milk and meat. The modern Brown Swiss gives a great deal of milk. The milk of Braunvieh has a lot of protein and is especially well suited to **cheesemaking**. Much Swiss cheese such as Appenzeller or mountain cheese is also made from Braunvieh milk.

Alongside the Simmental and the Holstein, the Braunvieh is one of the most important breeds of cow in Switzerland. Many Swiss link it with the typical picture of cows with bells on the alp. At the **descent from the alp** in autumn the cows are driven festively decorated into the valley. The breeders' association Braunvieh Schweiz has its seat in Zug and organises exhibitions and cattle shows.

begriffe.erklaerung: A group of animals of one species with similar appearance and characteristics.
The bare, moist skin on the nose and muzzle of a bovine.
Cattle that are kept for both milk and meat.
The festive driving of the cows from the alp down to the valley in autumn.

gewusst: The Braunvieh is also shown on many postcards and souvenirs as the typical Swiss cow.
Braunvieh from Switzerland was exported to the USA and later came back as Brown Swiss.

teile.einleitung: Anteaters are mammals from Central and South America that feed almost only on ants and termites. They have a long, tube-shaped snout, no teeth and an incredibly long, sticky tongue. The best known is the giant anteater with its bushy tail.
wichtigste: Anteaters live in Central and South America.
There are four species, and the largest is the giant anteater.
An adult giant anteater has no teeth.
Its tongue is altogether about 60 centimetres long.
It eats about 35,000 ants and termites a day.
Anteaters are related to sloths.
The giant anteater is considered vulnerable.

abschnitte.text: Anteaters form the suborder **Vermilingua**, which means worm tongue. They belong to the order Pilosa, and their closest relatives are the **sloths**. Together with the armadillos, they form the superorder of Xenarthra. They are not related to bears, despite their name. Carl von Linné was the first to describe the giant anteater scientifically in 1758 and named it Myrmecophaga tridactyla, that is, “ant eater with three fingers”, because of the three striking clawed fingers.

The **giant anteater** is about two metres long including the tail and usually weighs 20 to 40 kilograms. It has greyish-brown fur with a black stripe edged in white on the shoulder and a huge, bushy tail. The two **tamanduas** are smaller and climb well in trees. The silky anteater is only about as big as a squirrel and lives almost only in treetops. All species live in Central and South America, from Mexico to Argentina.

An adult giant anteater has **no teeth**. Instead it has a tongue that is altogether about 60 centimetres long. It is covered with sticky saliva and fine horny hooks on which the insects get stuck. Up to about 160 times a minute it flicks it out. In the stomach, sand and little stones grind up the prey, similar to a bird’s gizzard.

With its strong claws, the anteater tears open ant and termite nests. At one nest it usually eats for at most about a minute, then moves on. In this way it is not bitten too often, and the insect colony survives and grows back. Per day, a giant anteater eats about **35,000** ants and termites. Because this food supplies little energy, it has a low body temperature and sleeps a lot.

The giant anteater lives as a **loner** and walks on the knuckles of its front feet to protect its claws. To sleep, it covers itself with its large tail like a blanket. The female usually has a single young. The young animal rides for many months on the mother’s **back**, where it is well camouflaged by the striped fur. When threatened, it rears up and defends itself with its dangerous claws.

The giant anteater is considered **vulnerable**. Its habitats, grassland and forests, are being converted into farmland and pastures. Many animals die in fires or are run over on roads. In protected areas and zoo breeding programmes, attempts are made to preserve the species. You can also watch giant anteaters in zoos in Europe.

begriffe.erklaerung: A group of mammals in the Americas to which anteaters, sloths and armadillos belong.
Insects that, like ants, live in large colonies and often build huge mounds.
An animal that mostly lives alone and not in groups.
Long, hard, curved nails on the fingers or toes of an animal.

gewusst: The tongue of the giant anteater is anchored in the chest almost at the breastbone.
The giant anteater has one of the lowest body temperatures of all mammals, only about 33 degrees.
A giant anteater can even fend off a jaguar with its claws.

teile.einleitung: The African golden wolf is a slender wild dog from North and East Africa. For a long time it was thought to be the same golden jackal that also lives in Asia and Europe. Only genetic studies showed that it is a species of its own and is more closely related to wolves.
wichtigste: The African golden wolf is a species of dog from Africa.
Genetic studies showed that the African golden jackals are a species of their own.
This species was given the name African golden wolf in 2015.
It lives in North Africa, West Africa and East Africa.
It is smaller than a wolf and larger than a fox.
The golden wolf eats small animals, insects, fruit and also carrion.
It is not considered threatened.

abschnitte.text: In the past, the golden-brown wild dogs of Africa were counted as the **golden jackal**, which occurs from south-eastern Europe to Asia. In 2015, researchers compared the genetic material of these animals. It turned out that the African animals are not related to the golden jackal but more closely to the wolf and the coyote. That is why they were given the new name African golden wolf, scientifically **Canis lupaster**.

The African golden wolf has yellowish to greyish-brown fur with darker hairs on its back. It has long legs, large ears and a bushy tail with a dark tip. It usually weighs about 7 to 15 kilograms. That makes it about as large as a medium-sized **domestic dog**.

The golden wolf lives in many countries of Africa north of the equator, for example in Egypt, Morocco, Senegal, Ethiopia and Kenya. It occurs on desert edges, in savannas and in mountains. It also feels at home near villages. It is very **adaptable** and gets by with little water.

The golden wolf is an **omnivore** with a preference for meat. It hunts mice, hares, birds and insects and also eats fruit. It gladly takes carrion or waste from humans. Mostly it lives in pairs or small family groups that defend a **territory** together.

Its former relative, the golden jackal, has been spreading in Europe for a few decades. Since 2011 it has also been recorded again and again in Switzerland. It is not directly related to the African golden wolf, however, but only looks similar to it. Such cases show how important **genetics** is for classifying animals.

begriffe.erklaerung: The science of the genetic material that is in every cell.
A group of living things that can reproduce with one another.
An area that an animal or a group defends against others.
The building instructions of a living thing, stored in DNA.

gewusst: The African golden wolf was often depicted in ancient Egypt, and people think of the god Anubis with the dog’s head.
Although it is so widespread, it was recognised as a species of its own only in 2015.
The golden jackal that sometimes turns up in Switzerland today is a different species.

teile.einleitung: A beaver dam is a wall of branches, twigs and mud with which a beaver dams up a stream. Behind it a pond forms, the beaver pond. In this way the beaver transforms a whole landscape.
wichtigste: Beavers build dams mainly from branches, twigs and mud.
A dam raises the water level and so protects the entrance to the beaver lodge.
Behind the dam a beaver pond forms.
If a dam is damaged, the beavers usually repair it the same night.
The pond offers new habitat to many other animals.
Beavers build dams only where the water is too shallow.
Beaver dams can slow floods, but can also flood fields.

abschnitte.text: A beaver needs water that is at least about half a metre to a metre deep. Only then is the entrance to its lodge safely under water. If a stream is too shallow, it dams it up with a **beaver dam**. In deep water it can also swim to transport branches and hide from enemies. On large rivers and lakes beavers therefore usually do not build dams.

First the beaver pushes branches crosswise into the streambed. Then it stuffs twigs, stones, leaves and above all **mud** into the gaps. It carries the mud with its front paws held against its chest. In this way the dam becomes ever denser and higher. When the beaver hears water trickling, it looks for the leaking spot and seals it.

Most beaver dams are a few metres long and less than a metre high. Some dams, however, are extended over the years by several generations of beavers. The longest known beaver dam lies in Wood Buffalo National Park in Canada and is around 850 metres long. It is so big that it can be seen on satellite pictures.

Behind the dam a **beaver pond** forms. Soon frogs, newts, dragonflies, fish and water birds live in it. Dead trees in the water become homes for woodpeckers and beetles. Experts say that the beaver clearly increases the **biodiversity** along a stream. In addition, the pond holds back water in dry periods and slows the flood when there is heavy rain.

Sometimes a beaver dam backs water up onto meadows, fields or paths. In Switzerland the wildlife wardens and municipalities then look for solutions. Often a pipe is laid through the dam to limit the water level, which is called a **dam drain**. Simply tearing the dam down achieves little, because the beavers usually repair it the very next night.

begriffe.erklaerung: The pond that forms behind a beaver dam.
A pipe through a beaver dam that limits the water level.
How many different animal and plant species live in a place.

gewusst: Beavers react to the sound of flowing water and start building at once.
The longest beaver dam in the world is longer than eight football pitches.

teile.einleitung: The Atlantic salmon is a powerful migratory fish that grows up in the sea and returns to its home river to spawn. On this journey it even leaps over waterfalls. In the past it swam up the Rhine as far as Switzerland.
wichtigste: The Atlantic salmon is called Salmo salar scientifically and belongs to the bony fish.
It can grow to about 1.5 metres long.
Young salmon grow up in the river, adults live in the sea.
To spawn they migrate back to their home river and find it mainly by their sense of smell.
They often overcome waterfalls and weirs with powerful leaps.
In the past the Rhine was an important salmon river as far as Switzerland.
Norway is one of the biggest producers of farmed salmon.

abschnitte.text: The Atlantic salmon, in Latin **Salmo salar**, is a bony fish from the salmon family. It has a slim, silvery shiny body with small black spots. Large animals grow to about 1.5 metres long, but most stay considerably smaller. At spawning time the males turn reddish, and their lower jaw curves into a hook, and they are then called **hook-jawed salmon**.

Salmon hatch in gravelly rivers in the north of Europe and North America. The young fish are called **parr** and have dark marks on their sides that camouflage them well on the stream bed. After one to several years they turn silvery and swim to the sea. In the North Atlantic they eat mainly small fish and crustaceans and grow quickly.

After one or more years in the sea the salmon return to the river where they were born. This journey is called the **spawning migration**, and they recognise their home river mainly by its smell. On the way they overcome waterfalls and weirs with leaps of over a metre in height. During the migration they hardly eat anything and live on their fat reserves. Many animals die after spawning, but some return to the sea and spawn once more later.

In the sea, seals, large predatory fish and seabirds hunt the salmon. In the river otters, bears and herons are dangerous. Even greater are the problems caused by humans, such as **dams**, polluted water and overfishing. That is why wild salmon have become rare in many rivers.

Until the 19th century many salmon swam up the **Rhine** every year as far as Basel and on into the Aare and Limmat. Through the building of power stations, straightening of rivers and dirty water, the salmon disappeared from Switzerland in the 20th century. Today the countries along the Rhine are working to make the power stations passable with **fish ladders** so that the salmon can return. In Switzerland young salmon have already been released into streams for this purpose.

Almost all the salmon that you can buy in the shop comes from **aquaculture**. Norway is one of the largest producers, and Scotland and Chile also farm a lot of salmon. The fish grow up there in large net pens in the sea. Critics complain that diseases and escaped farmed salmon can harm the wild salmon.

begriffe.erklaerung: Laying eggs and fertilising them, in fish and amphibians.
A young salmon with dark marks that still lives in the river.
A male salmon at spawning time with a curved lower jaw.
A structure with steps and pools by which fish can swim around a weir.
The farming of fish or other water animals by people.

gewusst: The pink colour of salmon flesh comes from pigments in the crustaceans that the salmon eats.
In Basel there are said to have been so many salmon in the past that they counted as simple everyday food.
On its spawning migration a salmon can swim more than a thousand kilometres upstream.

teile.einleitung: Anadromy is a technical word for a special migration of fish. Anadromous fish grow up in the sea and swim up rivers to spawn, often into the very river where they were hatched themselves. The best-known example is the salmon.
wichtigste: Anadromous fish live in the sea and migrate into rivers to spawn.
The word comes from Greek and means roughly “running up”.
Typical anadromous fish are salmon, sea trout, allis shad, sturgeon and sea lamprey.
The opposite is called catadromous, as with the eel.
Salmon find their home river mainly with their sense of smell.
Dams and power stations block the way for many migratory fish.
In the past, salmon swam up the Rhine as far as Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: **Anadromy** means a migration from the sea upstream into fresh water in order to spawn there. The word is made up of the Greek parts ana, “up”, and dromos, “run”. The eggs are laid in rivers and streams, where the young fish hatch. Later the young fish migrate to the sea, where they find plenty of food and grow large. Fish with such migrations are called **migratory fish**.

The best-known example is the **Atlantic salmon**. Sea trout, allis shad, smelt, various **sturgeons** and the sea lamprey are also anadromous. In the Pacific there are several species of salmon, such as the sockeye and the Chinook. Pacific salmon die after spawning, while Atlantic salmon can return to the sea several times. In North America the dead salmon are an important food for bears and even fertilise the forests along the banks.

Salmon often live in the sea for several years and cover thousands of kilometres there. To spawn they usually return to exactly the river where they hatched. In the sea they probably find their way by the Earth's **magnetic field**. Near the coast they recognise their home river by the **smell** of the water. On the way upstream, salmon leap over rapids and small waterfalls.

abschnitte.titel: From salt water to fresh water
abschnitte.text: The change between sea and river is a great challenge for the body. In the sea a fish loses water, in fresh water it takes in too much water. Anadromous fish therefore adjust their gills and kidneys each time, which is called **osmoregulation**. Before their journey to the sea, young salmon even change colour and turn silvery. At this stage they are called smolts.

For **catadromous** fish it is exactly the other way round: they live in fresh water and spawn in the sea. The best-known example is the **European eel**. It grows up in rivers and lakes, including in Switzerland, and swims all the way to the Sargasso Sea in the Atlantic to spawn. Both kinds of migration are grouped together under the term diadromous.

In the past, many salmon swam up the Rhine every year as far as Basel and on into the Aare, Limmat and Reuss. Because of **power stations**, weirs and polluted water, the salmon disappeared from Switzerland in the middle of the 20th century. Today the countries along the Rhine are building **fish ladders** and fish passes so that migratory fish can get past the obstacles. Young salmon are released into Swiss streams so that one day the salmon will return. But until salmon from the sea swim into Switzerland regularly again, more fish passes are still needed.

begriffe.erklaerung: The laying of eggs by fish and amphibians.
A fish that travels back and forth between different bodies of water.
Living in fresh water and migrating to the sea to spawn, like the eel.
A structure with small pools that lets fish get around a weir or power station.

gewusst: Salmon can leap up waterfalls more than three metres high.
A single salmon can swim thousands of kilometres to return to the stream where it was born.
The sturgeon is an anadromous fish whose ancestors lived more than 100 million years ago.

teile.einleitung: Leafcutter ants are hard-working ants from the warm areas of the Americas. You recognise them by their long columns in which each ant carries a green piece of leaf above its head. From the leaves they make a garden in the nest in which a fungus grows.
wichtigste: Leafcutter ants carry pieces of leaf above their heads into the nest.
They do not eat the leaves, but grow fungi on them as food.
They live from the south of the USA to Argentina.
Their colonies can number several million animals.
Each ant has a particular job depending on its size.
Ants and fungus need each other to survive.

abschnitte.text: The ants climb on trees and bushes and with their **jaws** cut semicircular pieces out of the leaves. The jaws work like a small saw. After that they carry the piece of leaf high above their heads back to the nest. From a distance such an **ant trail** looks like a train of tiny green sails.

In the nest the leaves are cleaned, chewed small and made into a soft pulp. On it the ants plant pieces of their **fungus**. The fungus grows and forms small, nutrient-rich nodules that the ants eat. They tend their fungus garden carefully and remove harmful moulds. Without the ants this fungus could not live, and the ants could not live without it.

In a colony there are workers of very different sizes. The largest are **soldiers** with mighty heads who defend the nest. Medium-sized ones cut and carry leaves. The smallest look after the fungus garden and the brood, and some even ride along on pieces of leaf and protect the carrier from flies. At the top stands the **queen**, who lays all the eggs.

Leafcutter ants live only in the Americas, from the south of the USA to Argentina. They are most common in the rainforests of Central and South America. Their nests lie underground and can become huge. A large nest can take up an area as big as a classroom or more.

Leafcutter ants are important for the rainforest because they bring plant remains into the soil and loosen it. On plantations and fields, by contrast, they are often regarded as **pests**. Researchers study them because their cooperation is so well organised. In Switzerland you can watch them in zoos and tropical houses.

begriffe.erklaerung: The biting mouthparts of an ant.
A chamber in the nest in which the ants grow their fungus.
An especially large worker that defends the nest.
An ant society with a queen and many workers.

gewusst: Leafcutter ants were farmers long before there were humans.
Small ants sometimes ride along on the pieces of leaf to ward off parasites.
A large nest can contain so much soil that you would need a lorry to carry it away.

teile.einleitung: The bonobo is a great ape from the rainforest of Africa and a close relative of the chimpanzee. It is regarded as especially peaceful, because bonobos often settle arguments with hugs and comfort. Together with the chimpanzee it is our closest living relative.
wichtigste: Bonobos are great apes and closely related to chimpanzees.
They live only in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, south of the Congo River.
Fully grown bonobos weigh about 30 to 60 kilograms.
Their face is dark, and the lips are reddish.
Among bonobos the females have a lot of say.
They often settle arguments with body contact, comfort and attention.
Bonobos are highly endangered.

abschnitte.text: Bonobos are somewhat slimmer than chimpanzees and have longer legs. They are much smaller and lighter than **gorillas** and weigh about 30 to 60 kilograms. Their fur is black, and the face is dark with reddish lips. In many bonobos the hair on the head is parted in the middle, as if styled. On the ground they usually walk on all fours in **knuckle-walking**, but they can also walk upright.

Bonobos live only in the **Democratic Republic of the Congo** in central Africa. Their area lies south of the great Congo River, which they cannot cross. There they live in dense rainforests. They are active during the day and every evening build a sleeping nest of branches and leaves in the trees. Young bonobos usually sleep in the nest with their mother.

Bonobos eat mainly **fruit**. In addition there are leaves, seeds, fungi, insects and sometimes small animals. When foraging the group often splits into smaller groups. In the evening the groups meet again.

Bonobos live in communities of 10 to over 100 animals. Unlike in chimpanzees, the **females** have a lot of influence and stick together. When young females become adult, they usually leave the group they were born in, while the males stay. Bonobos often settle arguments with body contact, hugs and comfort instead of fights. They communicate with sounds, gestures and facial expressions.

Bonobos and chimpanzees are the closest living **relatives** of humans. Their genes match ours by almost 99 per cent. Only in 1929 was the bonobo described as a species of its own, before that it was thought to be a chimpanzee. Researchers have shown that bonobos use tools and can learn symbols.

Bonobos are **highly endangered**. Their forest is being cleared, and they are hunted because their meat is sold. In addition there are wars in the region that make protection harder. They are protected in protected areas and sanctuaries in the Congo. Zoos keep bonobos for conservation breeding and to draw people's attention to the species.

begriffe.erklaerung: A group of large apes without a tail: orangutans, gorillas, chimpanzees and bonobos.
Walking on all fours with the hands resting on the knuckles of the fingers.
Breeding in zoos so that an endangered species does not die out.
The blueprint of a living thing that is in every cell.

gewusst: Bonobos were only recognised as a species of their own in 1929, much later than the other great apes.
The Congo River separates bonobos and chimpanzees, because neither species can swim.
A bonobo called Kanzi learned to communicate with people using hundreds of picture symbols.

teile.einleitung: The Bodensee-Kilch was a species of whitefish that lived only in Lake Constance. It stayed at great depth and was rarely seen. Today it no longer exists: it has become extinct.
wichtigste: The Bodensee-Kilch was a species of whitefish that occurred only in Lake Constance.
Its scientific name is Coregonus gutturosus.
It lived in the deep parts of the lake.
It probably became extinct in the 1970s.
The main reason was over-fertilisation of the lake, which meant there was no oxygen in the depths.
The International Union for Conservation of Nature, IUCN, lists it as extinct.

abschnitte.text: The Kilch belonged to the **whitefish**, silvery fish from the salmon family. It grew to about 30 centimetres long and was rather small and light. Its back was olive green or brown, and its mouth sat slightly low on the blunt snout. It lived in the **depths** of Lake Constance, in winter at about 100 to 140 metres.

In summer the Kilch ate mussels and snails from the **lake bed**. In winter it fed on the spawn of the Blaufelchen. It laid its eggs between July and November at a depth of 10 to 60 metres. Because it lived so deep, it was only rarely caught.

When a Kilch was brought up from the depths, it often looked badly deformed. Its belly swelled up through the difference in pressure and could even burst. The same happens in many **deep-sea fish**. For the fishers it was therefore a special and rare catch.

From the 1950s a lot of sewage and fertiliser got into Lake Constance. This **over-fertilisation** made algae grow strongly. When the algae died and rotted on the bottom, this used up a lot of oxygen. On the lake bed the oxygen became so scarce that the eggs of many whitefish could no longer develop. Other species of whitefish recovered thanks to released young fish, but the Kilch probably vanished in the 1970s.

The Kilch shows how sensitive lakes are to pollution. In many Swiss lakes further **species of whitefish** became extinct in the same period. Today sewage treatment plants make sure that Lake Constance is clean again. Extinct species, however, do not come back. That is why it is so important to protect habitats before it is too late.

begriffe.erklaerung: A species of which not a single animal is still alive.
Too many nutrients in the water, as a result of which algae grow strongly.
The eggs of fish and frogs.
Silvery fish from the salmon family that live in cool lakes.

gewusst: The Kilch lived nowhere else in the world but in Lake Constance.
When a Kilch was pulled up from the depths, its belly could burst through the difference in pressure.
In winter the Kilch ate, of all things, the eggs of its relatives, the Blaufelchen.

teile.einleitung: The Appenzeller Spitzhauben are a well-known Swiss breed of chicken with a striking, pointed crest of feathers on the head. They come from the Appenzell region and are among the oldest breeds of chicken in Switzerland. With their cheeky tuft of feathers they look as if they were wearing a little hat.
wichtigste: The Appenzeller Spitzhauben is a well-known Swiss breed of chicken.
Typical is the pointed crest of feathers pointing forwards.
It comes from the Appenzell region in eastern Switzerland.
Instead of a large comb it has a small V-shaped comb.
The hens lay white eggs.
The chickens are light, hardy and good fliers.
Pro Specie Rara helps to preserve the breed.

abschnitte.text: The most striking feature is the pointed **crest of feathers** on the head, pointing forwards. Instead of a serrated comb the birds have a small, two-part **V-shaped comb** that looks like a V. The best-known colour is silver-spangled black, but there are also golden, black and blue birds. The chickens are slim and light and walk with a proud, upright gait.

The breed comes from the **Appenzell region** in eastern Switzerland and has been kept there for centuries. Its name comes from the Spitzhaube, a cap that used to be part of the traditional costume of Appenzell women. The chickens' crest of feathers is reminiscent of this headgear. This makes it a true Swiss breed of chicken.

A hen lays about 150 to 180 white eggs a year. A hen usually weighs only about 1.5 kilograms, a cockerel a little more. The breed is therefore not suited to producing a lot of meat. Today it is bred mainly by hobby keepers for its beauty and hardiness.

Appenzeller Spitzhauben are lively, curious and watchful chickens. They are very **hardy** and cope well with the rough mountain climate. Because they are light, they can fly well and like to perch in trees or on fences. They need plenty of room to roam, where they can scratch about and look for worms and grains.

In the 20th century the old native breeds became rarer and rarer, because high-performance chickens lay more eggs. Since the 1980s the foundation **Pro Specie Rara** has been working to preserve old Swiss breeds of farm animals, including the Appenzeller Spitzhauben. Thanks to dedicated breeders the breed is now secure again. At poultry shows in Switzerland it is a popular eye-catcher.

begriffe.erklaerung: A group of domestic animals of the same species with shared, bred characteristics.
A tuft of long feathers on the head of a bird.
A small comb made of two points that look like little horns.
A Swiss foundation that preserves old breeds of farm animals and cultivated plants.

gewusst: The crest of feathers can be so big that it takes away a little of the chickens' view.
There is a second Appenzell breed of chicken, the Appenzeller Barthuhn, which has a beard of feathers.
Appenzeller Spitzhauben fly so well that their run often has to be covered with a net.

teile.einleitung: The city of Bern and the bear have belonged together for centuries. The bear is the heraldic animal of the city and the canton of Bern and, according to legend, even gave the city its name. To this day real bears live in the middle of the federal city.
wichtigste: The bear is the heraldic animal of the city and the canton of Bern.
It has adorned the coat of arms for centuries and is linked with the name of the city.
According to legend, Duke Berchtold V of Zähringen named the city after a bear he had killed.
The city was founded in 1191.
For centuries Bern has kept live bears, in the past in the Bear Pit.
Since 2009 the bears have lived in the larger Bear Park on the bank of the Aare.

abschnitte.titel: The bear in the coat of arms
abschnitte.text: The Bernese **coat of arms** shows a black bear with a red tongue and red claws on a golden diagonal band on a red field. The bear can be seen on very old seals of the city from the 13th century. It adorns flags, fountains, buildings and souvenirs. The canton of Bern also uses the same coat of arms. In this way the bear has become the symbol of Bern.

Bern was founded in 1191 by Duke **Berchtold V of Zähringen**. According to legend, he wanted to name the city after the first animal killed on a hunt in the surrounding forests. This animal was a bear, and so the name Bern came about. Linguists consider it possible, however, that the name has another origin. The story of the bear is nevertheless the best-known **legend** of the city.

abschnitte.titel: From the Bear Pit to the Bear Park
abschnitte.text: As early as the Middle Ages Bern kept live bears in the city. The famous **Bear Pit** at the eastern end of the Old Town was opened in 1857. The bears lived there for a long time in a cramped, stony pit. In 2009 the much larger **Bear Park** was opened next to it, leading steeply down to the Aare. There the bears can dig, climb and bathe in the water.

In the Old Town of Bern, which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, you meet bears everywhere. The Zähringer Fountain shows a bear in knight's armour with a banner. At the Zytglogge tower, too, a procession of little figure bears passes by on every full hour. On many signs, flags and coats of arms the **heraldic animal** can be seen. For children a walk in search of bears is worthwhile.

The bears of Bern are **brown bears**, the largest predators in Europe. In the wild in Switzerland, brown bears were wiped out in the 19th and early 20th centuries. The last one was shot in 1904 in the Lower Engadine. Since 2005 individual young bears have been migrating again from Italy into the Grisons. Whether the bear will become native again in Switzerland is an open question.

begriffe.erklaerung: An animal that is shown on a coat of arms and represents a city or a country.
A sign with colours and pictures that stands for a family, a city or a country.
An old tale that does not necessarily have to be true.
A large bear with brown fur that lives in Europe, Asia and North America.

gewusst: A bear pit in Bern is already mentioned in the year 1513.
In dialect a Bernese bear is often called “Mutz”.
The Bear Park is freely accessible, and you can watch the bears without paying an entrance fee.

teile.einleitung: The Alpabzug is the moment in autumn when cows, goats and sheep come back from the Alp into the valley. In many Swiss villages it is celebrated with a colourful festival. The animals then often wear magnificent flower decorations and large bells.
wichtigste: When the animals come from the Alp into the valley in autumn, it is called the Alpabzug.
This applies to cows, goats and sheep.
The Alpabzug usually takes place in September or early October.
At traditional festivals the animals are decorated with flowers.
In French-speaking Switzerland the Alpabzug is called Désalpe.
Traditionally the animals are decorated only if no misfortune happened over the summer.
Many Alpabzüge today attract thousands of spectators.

abschnitte.text: After about 100 days on the Alp, it gets cold in the mountains, and the grass no longer grows. Then the Älpler (herdsmen) bring their animals back into the valley. This is called the **Alpabzug**, the descent from the Alp, or in French **Désalpe**. It usually takes place between the middle of September and the beginning of October.

For the Alpabzug, the animals are smartened up for the festival. The most beautiful cows wear a **headdress** of flowers, fir twigs and coloured ribbons. The lead cow often wears the largest bell, the **Treichel**. According to an old custom, the animals are decorated only if no animal and no person has had an accident all summer.

The Sennen and Sennerinnen (herdsmen and herdswomen) march along in their most beautiful **traditional costumes**. In some areas the men wear embroidered smocks or waistcoats. Often wagons with cheese, milk cauldrons and household goods follow at the back. Children help to drive goats or sheep.

Large Alpabzüge take place, for example, in Charmey in the canton of Fribourg, in Saint-Cergue in the canton of Vaud and in the Appenzellerland. They often include a market, music and specialities such as cheese and Älplermagronen (a Swiss dish of macaroni, potatoes and cheese). In the Valais, at the **Schafscheid** (the sheep sorting), the sheep are handed back to their owners after the alpine summer. Many festivals today attract thousands of guests from Switzerland and abroad.

Sheep and goat herds also return into the valley in autumn at the Alpabzug. Over the summer, sheep often graze freely in very high places and first have to be gathered together.
