Baboons, macaques and guenons belong to a group of monkeys that are also called **cheek-pouch monkeys**. With them they can quickly collect a lot when searching for food. Then they retreat to a safe place and eat in peace. That way they do not have to argue with their own kind or with enemies over every single fruit.

abschnitte.titel: Pouches on the outside of the head
abschnitte.text: In the North American **pocket gophers** and pocket mice the cheek pouches lie on the outside of the head. They are lined with fur and open beside the mouth. The animals can even turn them inside out to empty them. That way no soil stays in the mouth when they dig underground.

With cheek pouches an animal can collect a lot of food in a short time and so cut down the time outside when it is exposed to enemies. Animals that lay down **stores** especially benefit from them. The food is hardly digested in the pouches, because these produce no digestive juices. That is why the animals can later take it out again almost unchanged.

begriffe.erklaerung: A stretchy skin sac in the cheek for carrying food.
Food that an animal keeps for later, for example for the winter.
A group of monkeys to which baboons, macaques and guenons belong.
A North American rodent with fur-lined cheek pouches on the outside of its head.

gewusst: The German word “hamstern” for building up stores comes from the hamster and its stuffed cheeks.
The platypus also has cheek pouches in which it collects small animals it has found before it surfaces.

teile.einleitung: A calming signal is a sign in the body language of dogs with which they avoid arguments and calm themselves or others. When a dog yawns even though it is not tired at all, that can be such a sign. Anyone who knows these signals understands dogs much better.
wichtigste: Calming signals are signs of dog body language.
Dogs show them to avoid conflicts and to calm themselves.
Yawning without being tired can be a sign of stress or of calming.
Other signals are looking away, licking the nose and sniffing the ground.
The Norwegian dog trainer Turid Rugaas made the term well known.
Anyone who recognises the signals can give a stressed dog more peace.

abschnitte.text: Dogs cannot speak, but they communicate with their bodies. A **calming signal** is a small sign with which a dog shows: I do not want a fight. It uses it when a situation is unpleasant for it or when it wants to calm another dog or a person. Often it calms itself with it too. In English they are called **calming signals**.

A common signal is **yawning** even though the dog is not tired. Other signs are turning the head away, looking away, blinking or quickly licking the nose. Some dogs suddenly sniff the ground, sit down or walk towards someone in a curve. Slow movements or briefly freezing can also be part of it. Often a dog shows several signals one after another.

The term was made known by the Norwegian dog trainer **Turid Rugaas** in the 1990s. She watched many dogs and described about 30 such signals. Similar behaviour is also known from **wolves**, which have to avoid arguments within the pack. Not all researchers agree on which signs really serve to calm. What is clear, however, is that such signals often point to stress.

A dog is examined by the vet and yawns several times in a row. A child hugs a dog, and it turns its head away and licks its nose. Two strange dogs meet and do not walk straight at each other, but towards each other in a **curve**. In all these cases the dog is saying: this is too much for me right now. Anyone who recognises that can ease the situation.

Always ask the owner first before you stroke a strange dog. Do not walk straight at a dog and do not stare it in the eyes. Many dogs do not like being hugged, even if it is meant kindly. If a dog yawns, looks away or turns away, give it **space**. This way you avoid a stressed dog growling or snapping at some point.

begriffe.erklaerung: Communication through posture, movements and facial expression instead of with words.
Tension when a situation is unpleasant or threatening.
An argument or a clash.
A group of wolves or dogs that lives together.

gewusst: Dogs can also use their signals to try to calm people, for example when they argue loudly.
Many dog bites to children happen not with strange dogs, but with dogs that the child knows well.
A dog that pauses briefly during play and shakes itself often releases excitement in this way.

teile.einleitung: The Amazon is the river with the most water on Earth and flows right across South America. It flows through the largest rainforest in the world, in which jaguars, sloths, parrots and countless other animals live. No other river carries so much water into the sea.
wichtigste: The Amazon is the river with the most water in the world.
It is about 6,400 to 7,000 kilometres long, depending on the measurement.
It rises in the Andes in Peru and flows into the Atlantic in Brazil.
Around the river grows the Amazon rainforest, the largest rainforest on Earth.
In the Amazon region lives about one in ten of the known animal species in the world.
Jaguars, pink river dolphins, piranhas and anacondas live on the Amazon.
Deforestation and fires threaten the rainforest.

abschnitte.text: The **Amazon** rises high in the Andes in Peru and flows about 6,400 to 7,000 kilometres to the Atlantic. Whether it or the Nile is the longest river in the world, experts still argue about. What is certain: the Amazon carries by far the most water. At its mouth, on average over 200,000 cubic metres of water per second flow into the sea, more than the next seven largest rivers together. That is about a fifth of all the river water that reaches the sea worldwide.

The Amazon has over 1,000 **tributaries**, some of which are huge rivers themselves. At the city of Manaus, the black Rio Negro flows into the pale, muddy river. Because the two kinds of water differ in temperature and speed, they flow side by side for many kilometres without mixing. This is called the **Meeting of the Waters**. Near Belém the river flows into the Atlantic with a huge delta, and in the middle lies the island of Marajó, which is larger than Switzerland.

The catchment area of the Amazon covers about 7 million square kilometres, so over 150 times the area of Switzerland. The **rainforest** extends over nine countries, and most of it lies in Brazil. It is warm and damp all year round, and it rains a great deal. The trees store huge amounts of carbon and are therefore important for the climate of the whole world. Many parts of the forest are flooded every year during the rainy season.

In the Amazon region live especially many species, for example the **jaguar**, the largest big cat of the Americas. In the water swim pink river dolphins, piranhas, giant otters and the arapaima, one of the largest freshwater fish in the world. On the bank lurk caimans and anacondas. In the treetops live sloths, howler monkeys, toucans and colourful macaws. Every year researchers discover new species of plants and animals here.

For thousands of years, **indigenous peoples** have lived on the Amazon, and many of them still do. The Spaniard Francisco de Orellana travelled the river in 1541 and 1542 as the first European all the way to the mouth. The river got its name from the Amazons, warlike women from Greek legends. The largest city in the Amazon region is Manaus in Brazil, with over two million people. On the river, large ships travel far into the interior.

Since the 1970s, large parts of the forest have been cleared for **cattle pastures**, soya fields, timber and mining. In addition there are fires and longer dry periods through climate change. Experts fear that parts of the rainforest could turn into a savanna if too much forest is lost. Nature reserves and protected areas of the indigenous peoples help to preserve the forest. When shopping in Switzerland, too, you can look out for products without rainforest clearance.

begriffe.erklaerung: The whole area from which rainwater flows into a river and its tributaries.
A river that flows into a larger river.
A dense forest in warm regions in which it rains a lot almost all year.
The original inhabitants of an area.

gewusst: Not a single bridge crosses the whole Amazon.
In floods, the water level of the Amazon can rise by over ten metres in some places.
At certain tides, a huge wave runs from the sea upriver, the Pororoca, on which people even surf.

teile.einleitung: A biotope network links individual habitats of animals and plants with each other. Along hedges, strips of woodland, streams or wildlife bridges, animals can move from one area to the next. In this way small, isolated protected areas become a large network.
wichtigste: A biotope network links separate habitats into a network.
Connecting strips for animals are also called wildlife corridors.
In Central and South America jaguar territories are linked by strips of forest.
Roads, settlements and large fields cut up the habitats of many animals.
Green bridges help animals to cross motorways safely.
Isolated groups of animals are more prone to inbreeding and extinction.
In Switzerland there are hundreds of wildlife corridors of national importance.

abschnitte.text: A **biotope** is a habitat, for example a pond, a nutrient-poor meadow or a forest. Many animals have to move between such habitats to find food, partners or a new territory. A **biotope network** makes sure that these habitats are linked with each other. You can imagine it like a road network for animals and plants.

Motorways, railway lines, settlements and large fields cut up the landscape. This is called **fragmentation**. Animals such as roe deer, lynxes, toads or hedgehogs are run over on roads or can no longer get across at all. If a small group of animals stays trapped on an island, only related animals mate. This inbreeding makes the group weaker, and it can die out more easily.

A biotope network consists of large **core areas** and links between them. Links can be hedges, strips of woodland, near-natural streams or flower strips at the edge of a field. Small biotopes in between act like stepping stones in a stream. Over motorways run **green bridges**, and under roads there are tubes for amphibians and badgers. Fences guide the animals to these crossings.

The **jaguar** needs very large territories. In Central and South America, however, its forests are often separated by fields and pastures. Conservation organisations are therefore working on a jaguar corridor that is meant to link areas from Mexico to Argentina. In doing so, strips of forest are preserved or newly planted so that the big cats can travel. At the same time work is done with farmers so that conflicts with livestock decrease.

In Switzerland the Federal Office for the Environment has designated several hundred **wildlife corridors** of national importance. Many of them are interrupted by roads. For some years now the Confederation has therefore been building wildlife bridges over motorways, for example on the Central Plateau. The aim is an **ecological infrastructure**, a nationwide network of protected areas and links. Municipalities, farmers and private individuals can also help with hedges and flower strips.

A well-known example in Europe is the **Green Belt** along the former Iron Curtain. Where the border between East and West used to run, a long strip of nature was preserved. Today it links habitats from the Arctic Ocean to the Black Sea. In North America the Yellowstone to Yukon initiative works so that bears and wolves can travel over thousands of kilometres.

begriffe.erklaerung: A habitat in which certain animals and plants live.
A connecting strip along which wild animals travel from one habitat to another.
A planted bridge over a road that is intended only for animals.
When roads and settlements divide habitats into small pieces.

gewusst: Cameras on green bridges show that roe deer, foxes, badgers and even lynxes cross them at night.
In spring, fences are put up on some roads for toads so that they can reach their spawning waters safely.

teile.einleitung: The Appenzeller Spitzhauben chicken is a well-known Swiss breed of chicken with a striking crest of feathers on the head. The crest points forwards and is reminiscent of the headgear of the old Appenzell women's costume. The chicken is light, nimble and used to life in the mountains.
wichtigste: The Appenzeller Spitzhauben chicken is a well-known Swiss breed of chicken.
On its head it wears a striking, pointed crest of feathers.
The name comes from a cap of the Appenzell women's costume.
The best-known colour is silver-spangled black.
A hen lays about 150 to 180 white eggs a year.
The birds are weatherproof and like to fly up into trees.
The breed is one of the old Swiss breeds of farm animals.

abschnitte.text: The most striking feature is the pointed **crest of feathers** on the head, pointing forwards. Instead of a serrated comb the birds have a small, two-part **V-shaped comb** that looks like a V. The best-known colour is silver-spangled black, but there are also golden, black and blue birds. The chickens are slim and light and walk with a proud, upright gait.

The breed comes from the **Appenzell region** in eastern Switzerland and has been kept there for centuries. Its name comes from the Spitzhaube, a cap that used to be part of the traditional costume of Appenzell women. The chickens' crest of feathers is reminiscent of this headgear. This makes it a true Swiss breed of chicken.

A hen lays about 150 to 180 white eggs a year. A hen usually weighs only about 1.5 kilograms, a cockerel a little more. The breed is therefore not suited to producing a lot of meat. Today it is bred mainly by hobby keepers for its beauty and hardiness.

Appenzeller Spitzhauben are lively, curious and watchful chickens. They are very **hardy** and cope well with the rough mountain climate. Because they are light, they can fly well and like to perch in trees or on fences. They need plenty of room to roam, where they can scratch about and look for worms and grains.

In the 20th century the old native breeds became rarer and rarer, because high-performance chickens lay more eggs. Since the 1980s the foundation **Pro Specie Rara** has been working to preserve old Swiss breeds of farm animals, including the Appenzeller Spitzhauben. Thanks to dedicated breeders the breed is now secure again. At poultry shows in Switzerland it is a popular eye-catcher.

begriffe.erklaerung: A group of domestic animals of the same species with shared, bred characteristics.
A tuft of long feathers on the head of a bird.
A small comb made of two points that look like little horns.
A Swiss foundation that preserves old breeds of farm animals and cultivated plants.

gewusst: The crest of feathers can be so big that it takes away a little of the chickens' view.
There is a second Appenzell breed of chicken, the Appenzeller Barthuhn, which has a beard of feathers.
Appenzeller Spitzhauben fly so well that their run often has to be covered with a net.

teile.einleitung: The red admiral is a striking butterfly with almost black wings, a dark red band and white spots. Here you often see it in late summer on flowers or on windfall fruit. Especially exciting: many red admirals are migrating butterflies that fly across the Alps.
wichtigste: The red admiral has dark wings with dark red bands and white spots.
It belongs to the family of the brush-footed butterflies.
Its wingspan is about 5 to 6 centimetres.
The caterpillars eat mainly stinging nettles.
The red admiral is a migrating butterfly that flies to us from the south every year.
Adult butterflies like to drink the juice of rotting fruit.
The scientific name is Vanessa atalanta.

abschnitte.text: The upper side of the wings is velvety blackish brown. Across the forewings runs a **red band**, and at the tips sit white spots. The hindwings also have a red edge. The underside, by contrast, is marbled brown, so with its wings folded shut the butterfly is well camouflaged.

The red admiral lives in Europe, North Africa, parts of Asia and North America. You find it in gardens, at the edges of woods and on meadows. In Switzerland it occurs from the lowlands up high into the mountains. It belongs to the **brush-footed butterflies**, like the painted lady and the peacock butterfly.

Many red admirals spend the winter around the Mediterranean. In spring they fly north and even cross the **Alps** on the way. Here they lay eggs, and the next generation flies south again in autumn. Because of the milder winters, however, more and more red admirals now also spend the winter with us.

The female lays her eggs singly on the leaves of the **stinging nettle**. The caterpillar is dark and spiny and builds itself a small tent from a leaf spun together. In it, it is protected from birds. After a few weeks it pupates, and a new butterfly hatches from the pupa.

Adult red admirals suck nectar from flowers such as butterfly bush or thistles. In autumn they like to visit flowering ivy. Even more gladly they drink the sweet juice of overripe **windfall fruit** such as apples, pears or Zwetschgen (plums). For this they use their long proboscis, which they roll up like a garden hose.

The red admiral is not threatened in Switzerland. Even so, gardens close to nature help it. Anyone who leaves a corner with **stinging nettles** standing creates food for the caterpillars. Windfall fruit under the trees is also a welcome buffet for many butterflies in autumn.

begriffe.erklaerung: A large family of butterflies to which the red admiral also belongs.
A butterfly that flies long distances between its summer and winter areas.
The resting phase in which the caterpillar changes into a butterfly.
The long, roll-up mouth with which butterflies drink.

gewusst: On their migrations, red admirals can fly hundreds of kilometres.
Butterflies taste with their feet.
The caterpillar of the red admiral eats the stinging nettle without being bothered by the stinging hairs.

teile.einleitung: African elephants are the largest land animals on Earth. They include two species: the African savanna elephant and the smaller forest elephant. Their trunk is a true marvel of a tool, with which they grasp, drink and smell.
wichtigste: Two species belong to the African elephants.
The African elephant or bush elephant lives mainly in savannas.
The African forest elephant is smaller and lives in the rainforests of Central and West Africa.
The elephant uses its trunk for grasping, drinking and smelling.
African elephants have larger ears than Asian elephants.
Both species are threatened by poaching and loss of habitat.
Elephants live in herds led by an experienced cow.

abschnitte.text: For a long time it was thought that there was only one species of African elephant. Genetic studies showed, however, that the **forest elephant** is a species of its own. The bush elephant is larger and has curved tusks. The forest elephant is smaller, has rounder ears and straight tusks pointing downwards.

The **trunk** is a nose grown together with the upper lip. It consists of tens of thousands of muscle bundles and has not a single bone. With it the elephant grasps grass, branches or fruit, sucks up water and squirts it into its mouth. It also uses it to smell water and enemies from a great distance.

African elephants live in many countries south of the Sahara. Bush elephants inhabit savannas, bushland and open woodland, for example in Botswana, Kenya or Tanzania. Forest elephants live hidden in the **rainforests** of the Congo Basin. There they are hard to observe and therefore less well studied.

Elephants eat large amounts of plants and pass the seeds out again in their dung. In this way they spread many trees over long distances. Forest elephants are therefore regarded as important **gardeners of the rainforest**. With their feet and tusks they also dig waterholes, from which other animals drink too.

Because of their **ivory**, elephants were hunted heavily for a long time. Since 1989, the international trade in ivory has been largely banned. Even so, poaching continues, and fields and villages take habitat away from the elephants. The International Union for Conservation of Nature classes the bush elephant as endangered and the forest elephant as critically endangered.

begriffe.erklaerung: Greatly lengthened incisor teeth that stick out of the mouth.
The material of the tusks, which used to be used for jewellery and piano keys.
Illegal hunting of protected animals.
A wide grassland with scattered trees.

gewusst: With its trunk, an elephant can suck up several litres of water at once.
Elephants can communicate through deep rumbling sounds that humans cannot hear at all.
Forest elephants were officially classed as a species of their own, threatened with extinction, only in 2021.

teile.einleitung: The chacma baboon is the largest species of baboon and lives in southern Africa. It is a very adaptable monkey that occurs in savannas, mountains and even on coasts. It is also known for stealing tourists' food in some areas.
wichtigste: The chacma baboon is the largest species of baboon.
It lives in southern Africa.
Its scientific name is Papio ursinus.
Chacma baboons live in large groups that are called troops.
They are omnivores and eat fruit, grasses, roots, insects and small animals.
Like other baboons, they keep food in their cheek pouches.

abschnitte.text: The chacma baboon, in Latin **Papio ursinus**, is the largest species among the **baboons**. The males can weigh over 30 kilograms and are about twice as heavy as the females. Their fur is dark grey-brown, the face long and dog-like. The name ursinus means bear-like and refers to the dark, powerful appearance.

Chacma baboons live in **southern Africa**, including South Africa, Namibia, Botswana, Zimbabwe and Mozambique. They live in savannas, semi-deserts, mountains, forests and on coasts. What matters is that there is water and safe sleeping places. At night they sleep on steep **rock faces** or tall trees, where leopards can hardly reach them.

Chacma baboons are **omnivores**. They eat fruit, seeds, grasses, roots, insects and scorpions, sometimes also birds' eggs or young antelopes. On the coasts at the Cape, some groups even look for mussels and crabs. They use their **cheek pouches** to collect food quickly and eat it later in peace.

Chacma baboons live in troops of usually 20 to 80 animals, sometimes more. In the group there is a **pecking order** that is worked out through threats, fights and friendships. Grooming each other is very important for keeping up friendships. In the first months the young ride on their mother's back or hang from her belly.

Around **Cape Town** and at the Cape of Good Hope, some baboons have learned to search cars, houses and picnics for food. This often leads to conflicts with people. That is why there are baboon rangers there who keep the animals away from settlements. Tourists should never feed baboons and should keep food well closed.

begriffe.erklaerung: A large monkey of Africa that lives on the ground and has a dog-like snout.
A group of baboons that lives and travels together.
The order in an animal group of who is stronger or more important.
Cleaning each other's fur, which strengthens friendships.

gewusst: Chacma baboons can open car doors and get into houses when they smell food.
Their English name Chacma comes from the language of the Khoikhoi in southern Africa.

teile.einleitung: The Blaufelchen is a silvery shining fish that lives in Lake Constance. It belongs to the whitefish and is one of the most important food fish at the lake. It probably gets its name from its bluish shimmering back.
wichtigste: The Blaufelchen is a fish from the salmon family.
It is especially well known from Lake Constance.
The name probably comes from the bluish shimmering back.
It lives in open water and eats plankton.
After spawning the eggs sink to the lake bed.
Professional fishers catch it with floating nets.
Today fewer whitefish are caught than in the past, because the lake is poorer in nutrients.

abschnitte.text: The Blaufelchen has a slim, silvery body with small scales. Its back shimmers **bluish**, which is probably where its name comes from. Like all **salmon fish** it has a small adipose fin between the dorsal fin and the tail. The mouth is small, because it eats only tiny animals. Adult animals are usually about 30 to 40 centimetres long.

The Blaufelchen lives in the **open water** of Lake Constance, that is far away from the shore. There it travels about in large shoals. During the day it often stays in deeper layers, and in the evening it rises closer to the surface. Lake Constance borders Switzerland, Germany and Austria.

Blaufelchen eat mainly **zooplankton**, that is tiny crustaceans such as water fleas. They filter these out of the water with their fine gill rakers. How much food there is depends on how many nutrients are in the lake. Since Lake Constance has become cleaner and poorer in nutrients, less plankton grows. That is why the whitefish also grow more slowly.

Blaufelchen spawn in winter, usually in December. They release their eggs in the middle of open water. The eggs then sink slowly to the **lake bed** and develop there. In late winter or spring the tiny larvae hatch.

For centuries the Blaufelchen has been the bread-and-butter fish of the **professional fishers** on Lake Constance. They catch it with floating nets that hang in open water. In recent years catches have fallen sharply, also because of the nutrient-poor water and introduced species such as the stickleback. So that there are enough whitefish, eggs are hatched in fish hatcheries and young fish are released.

begriffe.erklaerung: A group of silvery fish that live in cool lakes.
Tiny living things that drift in the water.
When fish lay their eggs.
A fishing net that hangs in open water.

gewusst: In Switzerland whitefish are also called Balchen, Albeli or Bondelle depending on the region.
A single female whitefish can lay tens of thousands of eggs.
Whitefish fillets are a popular speciality in restaurants on Lake Constance.

teile.einleitung: The blackbird is one of the best-known birds in Switzerland. The male is black with a bright orange-yellow beak. With its beautiful, fluting song it often wakes us at first light.
wichtigste: The blackbird belongs to the thrush family.
The male is black, the female dark brown.
Many males have a yellow ring around the eyes.
Blackbirds live in gardens, parks and woods.
In summer they especially like to eat worms and insects, in autumn berries.
A blackbird raises two to three broods a year.
Many Swiss blackbirds stay nearby in winter.

abschnitte.text: The **blackbird** (Turdus merula) is about 24 to 27 centimetres long and weighs around 100 grams. The male is all black and has a bright orange-yellow **beak**. Many males wear a yellow ring around the eyes. The female is dark brown with a slightly spotted breast, which makes her better camouflaged on the nest. The legs are dark brown to blackish.

Originally the blackbird was a shy **woodland bird**. In the 19th century it began to move into towns and villages. Today in Switzerland it mostly lives in gardens, parks, cemeteries and woods. It is one of the best-known and most common garden birds. You can find it from the lowlands up to the mountain forests.

In summer blackbirds especially like to eat **earthworms**, insects, larvae and snails. You often see them hopping across the lawn, tilting their head to one side and then striking in a flash. In autumn and winter they eat many berries and fruits, for example elder, rowan berries and apples. In doing so they spread the seeds of shrubs. When they search through dry leaves you often hear a soft rustling.

In spring the male sings from high places such as roof ridges, aerials and treetops. His **song** is loud, fluting and melodic. The blackbird is often one of the first to sing at first light, and it also sings in the evening twilight. When danger threatens, it calls loudly and quickly “tix-tix-tix”. When it flies off in alarm, you often hear a shrill chattering.

The female builds a nest of grass, twigs and earth in hedges, trees or even on house walls. She usually lays four to five blue-green, speckled eggs. After about two weeks the young hatch, and both parents feed them. After around two more weeks the young birds leave the nest before they can really fly, and are then called **fledglings**. A blackbird can raise young two to three times a year.

In Switzerland the blackbird is a **resident bird** or partial migrant. Many birds stay nearby in winter or only travel short distances, and they do not fly far into Africa. Their enemies include house cats, sparrowhawks, magpies and crows. Since about 2016, in some summers many blackbirds in Switzerland have died of the **Usutu virus**, which is spread by mosquitoes. With hedges, bushes and a garden close to nature you can help blackbirds.

begriffe.erklaerung: A family of songbirds that includes the blackbird, the song thrush and the fieldfare.
A bird that stays in the same area all year round.
A young bird that has left the nest but cannot yet fly well.
A disease-causing germ that is spread by mosquitoes and can kill many blackbirds.

gewusst: Blackbirds in towns often sing earlier in the morning than in the woods, because it is brighter and noisier there.
There are also blackbirds with white feathers, which happens because of a disturbance in the making of pigment.
Some blackbirds copy other birds or even mobile phone ringtones in their song.

teile.einleitung: The Appenzell goat is a Swiss breed of goat from eastern Switzerland with a snow-white coat. Typical of it are the upright ears. At the cattle processions up to the mountain pastures in the Appenzell region, the white goats often walk proudly at the head of the procession.
wichtigste: The Appenzell goat is a Swiss breed of goat.
Its coat is entirely white.
Typical are the upright ears.
Most animals have no horns.
It is kept mainly for its milk.
At the procession up to the mountain pastures in the Appenzell region the goats often lead the way.
The breed was rare and is supported by Pro Specie Rara.

abschnitte.text: The Appenzell goat has a **white** coat that is often quite long. Especially on the hind legs, the long hair forms a kind of trousers. The ears stand upright and point slightly forwards. Most animals are **hornless**, that is, born without horns. A full-grown nanny goat (“Geiss”) weighs about 45 kilograms, a billy goat considerably more.

The breed comes from the cantons of **Appenzell Innerrhoden** and Appenzell Ausserrhoden and from the area around St Gallen. Farming families there have kept white goats for a long time. The animals are well adapted to the hilly and steep terrain. They climb surely and find enough food even on steep slopes.

Appenzell goats are good **dairy goats**. A nanny goat gives several hundred litres of milk a year. From goat's milk you can make cheese, yoghurt and other dairy products. Goats also help to keep pastures open, because they eat bushes and shrubs as well.

A special moment is the **procession up to the mountain pastures** (“Alpfahrt”) in early summer, when the cattle move up to the high pasture. In the Appenzell region the white goats often walk at the front. They are accompanied by a child in traditional costume, the “Geissbub” or “Geissmeitli”, the goat boy or goat girl. Behind them follow the herdsmen in their festive costume and the cows with large bells.

In the 20th century the Appenzell goat became rarer and rarer, because other breeds gave more milk. The foundation **Pro Specie Rara** took the breed into its conservation programme. Today many farms are breeding this goat again. It is a piece of living cultural heritage of eastern Switzerland.

begriffe.erklaerung: The Swiss word for a female goat.
A male goat.
Without horns, as many Appenzell goats are by nature.
The procession in which the animals are taken up to the mountain pastures in early summer.

gewusst: Goats are among the oldest domestic animals and were tamed some 10,000 years ago.
Goats like to eat buds and leaves from shrubs and even stand on their hind legs to reach them.
The white goats at the head of the Appenzell procession up to the mountain pastures are a popular photo subject.

teile.einleitung: The African penguin, also called the jackass penguin or spectacled penguin, is the only penguin that breeds in Africa. In German it is called the Brillenpinguin because of the black and white marking on its face, which around the eyes looks like a pair of spectacles. Because it calls as loudly as a donkey, it is also called the donkey penguin.
wichtigste: The African penguin lives on the coasts of South Africa and Namibia.
Around the eyes it has a black marking that looks like spectacles.
It grows to about 60 to 70 centimetres.
It eats mainly small shoaling fish such as sardines and anchovies.
Its calls sound like the braying of a donkey.
It is threatened with extinction today.

abschnitte.text: The African penguin has a black back and a white belly with a black band that runs across the chest like a horseshoe. On the face a black area frames the eyes, with a white arc above it, which together look like **spectacles**. Above the eyes it has bare, pink patches of skin that help it to give off surplus heat. Every animal has its own pattern of black dots on the chest, almost like a fingerprint.

African penguins live on the south-west coast of Africa, from Namibia to South Africa. There it is not icy cold, but the sea is rich in fish thanks to the cool **Benguela Current**. Well known is the colony on Boulders Beach near Cape Town, where people can get very close to the penguins. Most colonies, however, lie on small islands off the coast.

African penguins hunt in the sea for shoaling fish such as **sardines** and anchovies, sometimes also for squid. Under water they are very fast and agile, and their wings work like flippers. They usually dive only a few dozen metres deep. They often hunt in groups and drive the shoals of fish together.

African penguins usually live with the same partner for life. They build their nests in burrows, under bushes or in hollows, which in the past they dug into thick layers of old bird droppings. The female usually lays two eggs, and both parents take turns to incubate them for about 40 days. The chicks are also fed by both parents.

The number of African penguins has shrunk very sharply over the last hundred years. Reasons are the **overfishing** of their food fish, oil pollution and the earlier mining of bird droppings as fertiliser, through which nesting sites were lost. Today the species is listed on the Red List as threatened with extinction. Protected areas, artificial nest burrows and rescue stations for oiled birds are meant to help.

begriffe.erklaerung: A large group of animals that breed together in one place.
A cold, fish-rich ocean current off the west coast of southern Africa.
When people catch more fish than can grow back.
A list that shows how strongly animal and plant species are endangered.

gewusst: Because of its donkey-like cries the African penguin is also called the donkey penguin.
The dots on the chest are different in every African penguin, so researchers can recognise individual animals.
African penguins live in a climate in which it can get really hot in summer.

teile.einleitung: The Andes are the longest mountain range in the world above sea level. They run like a giant backbone along the whole west coast of South America. Llamas come from here, the Incas lived here and here stands the highest mountain outside Asia.
wichtigste: The Andes are about 7,500 kilometres long.
They stretch through seven countries, from Venezuela to Chile and Argentina.
The highest mountain is Aconcagua in Argentina at 6,961 metres.
There are many active volcanoes in the Andes.
Llamas, alpacas, vicuñas and the Andean condor live here.
The Inca Empire had its centre in the Andes.
Potatoes originally come from the Andes.

abschnitte.text: The **Andes** stretch about 7,500 kilometres from the Caribbean coast in the north to Tierra del Fuego in the south. That is about seven times as long as the Alps. They pass through Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, Chile and Argentina. In places the Andes are more than 500 kilometres wide. In Peru and Bolivia the high plateau called the **Altiplano** lies between two mountain chains.

The highest mountain in the Andes is **Aconcagua** in Argentina at 6,961 metres. It is the highest mountain outside Asia. The Andes are formed because the Nazca Plate is pushing under the South American continent. That is why there are many **volcanoes** and earthquakes here, for example Cotopaxi in Ecuador. The summit of Chimborazo in Ecuador is the point on the Earth's surface that is farthest from the centre of the Earth.

The Andes have very different landscapes, from rainforests and glaciers to deserts. In the north the mountain slopes are damp and green. On the border between Chile and Peru lies the **Atacama**, one of the driest deserts on Earth. Right in the south, in Patagonia, there are huge glaciers and ice fields. At great heights it is cold, and the air contains little oxygen.

**Llamas** and alpacas originally live in the Andes, and they are descended from the wild guanacos and vicuñas. Llamas have been used as pack animals for thousands of years, alpacas mainly for their wool. Above the peaks soars the **Andean condor**, one of the largest flying birds with a wingspan of around three metres. Other residents are the spectacled bear, the chinchilla and many species of hummingbird. Some of these animals are found nowhere else.

In the 15th and early 16th centuries the **Incas** ruled a large empire in the Andes with its capital at Cusco in Peru. The ruined city of **Machu Picchu**, high above a valley, is famous. The Incas built terraced fields and a long network of roads through the mountains. To this day many people in the Andes speak Quechua or Aymara. Potatoes, quinoa and tomatoes originally come from this region.

Some of the highest cities in the world lie in the Andes. La Paz in Bolivia lies at about 3,600 metres, Quito in Ecuador at around 2,800 metres. The people in the high regions have adapted to the thin air. Copper, silver, gold and lithium are mined in the mountains. For mountaineers, including those from Switzerland, the Andes are a popular destination.

begriffe.erklaerung: A long chain of high mountains.
A mountain from which hot, liquid rock, called lava, can escape.
A huge piece of the Earth's crust that moves very slowly.
A people who ruled a large empire in the Andes more than 500 years ago.

gewusst: The summit of Chimborazo is farther from the centre of the Earth than the summit of Mount Everest, because the Earth is thicker at the equator.
The Incas sent messages with runners who took turns along their mountain roads.
A llama spits when it is annoyed, but mostly at other llamas.

teile.einleitung: Arachnology is the science that deals with spiders and their relatives. People who do research in this field study how spiders are built, how they live and how they weave their webs. The name comes from the Greek word “arachne” for spider.
wichtigste: Arachnology is the science of spiders and arachnids.
Researchers in this field are called arachnologists.
Besides spiders, arachnids include scorpions, harvestmen and mites.
More than 50,000 species of spider have been described worldwide.
Around 1,000 species of spider live in Switzerland.
Arachnologists also study spider silk and spider venoms.
Arachnology is a branch of zoology.

abschnitte.text: **Arachnology** is a branch of zoology, the study of animals. It deals with the **arachnids**, which have eight legs and a two-part body. They include web-building spiders, scorpions, harvestmen, pseudoscorpions and mites. Insects such as beetles or flies are not included, because they have only six legs.

Arachnologists collect spiders in nature, for example with traps on the ground or by tapping branches. With the **microscope** they study fine features such as eyes, hairs and reproductive organs, by which species are told apart. Today analyses of DNA also help to tell related species apart. Every year, hundreds of new species of spider are still discovered.

A major research topic is **spider silk**, which, in proportion to its weight, is stronger than steel. Researchers hope to make new materials for medicine and technology from it one day. **Spider venoms** are also studied, because some substances in them may be useful as medicines. Other arachnologists observe how spiders hunt, build webs or look after their young.

The name goes back to the Greek legend of **Arachne**, a weaver who was turned into a spider by the goddess Athena. An important milestone was the book “Svenska Spindlar” by the Swede Carl Alexander Clerck from 1757. In it, spiders were for the first time given scientific names according to the system that is usual today. Today the World Spider Catalog at the Natural History Museum of Bern collects all the known species of spider in the world.

Around 1,000 species of spider occur in Switzerland. Well known are the **garden spider**, the house spider and the cellar spider. No native spider is dangerous to people. Spiders are useful because they eat very many insects such as mosquitoes and flies.

begriffe.erklaerung: The science of spiders and their relatives.
Animals with eight legs, for example spiders, scorpions and mites.
The science that deals with animals.
A great fear of spiders.

gewusst: The World Spider Catalog, the most important list of all spider species, is looked after in Bern.
The fear of spiders is called arachnophobia and is one of the most common fears.
All the spiders in the world together are estimated to eat hundreds of millions of tonnes of insects every year.

teile.einleitung: The Bezoar goat is a wild goat from the mountains of Western Asia. Our domestic goat descends from it and was tamed about 10,000 years ago. The males carry impressive horns that curve backwards like sabres.
wichtigste: The Bezoar goat is the ancestor of our domestic goat.
It lives in the mountains from Turkey across the Caucasus to Iran and Pakistan.
The domestic goat was tamed about 10,000 years ago in the area of the Fertile Crescent.
The males carry long, sabre-shaped horns with a sharp front edge.
The males have a dark beard on the chin.
It gets its name from the bezoar stones from its stomach.
Today it is regarded as endangered.

abschnitte.text: The Bezoar goat is a strong, agile mountain animal. The males are much bigger than the females and have grey-brown fur with dark stripes on the neck, shoulders and legs. They carry a dark beard on the chin. Their **horns** curve backwards like a sabre, have a sharp edge with knots at the front and can grow to over a metre long. The females, the **nannies**, have only short, thin horns.

Bezoar goats live in rocky, steep mountains and hills with little forest. Their range extends from Turkey across the **Caucasus** and Iran to Afghanistan and Pakistan. On some Mediterranean islands, such as Crete, there are also wild goats that are counted as this species. They climb very surely over rocks and scree. In winter they often move to lower altitudes.

Bezoar goats eat grasses, herbs, leaves and twigs of bushes. They live in **herds**, with the males and the nannies with their young often separate outside the mating season. In the mating season in autumn the males fight with their horns over the females. In spring the nanny gives birth to one or two young, which can climb after a short time. Enemies are wolves, leopards and large birds of prey.

abschnitte.titel: From wild goat to domestic goat
abschnitte.text: About 10,000 years ago people in the **Fertile Crescent**, especially in the Zagros Mountains in present-day Iran, began to keep Bezoar goats. This makes the goat one of the very first **domestic animals**, alongside the dog and the sheep. The goats provided milk, meat, wool and leather. With the farmers the domestic goat spread to Europe, Africa and Asia. Today there are very many breeds of goat worldwide, in Switzerland for example the Saanen goat and the Valais Blackneck goat.

The name comes from the **bezoar stones**, balls of matted hair and plant fibres that can form in the stomach of the animals. In the past people believed that such stones would help against poison, and they were very valuable. Today the Bezoar goat is **endangered** through hunting and competition with domestic goats for pasture. A close relative in Switzerland is the Alpine ibex. It too belongs to the genus of goats.

begriffe.erklaerung: A wild animal species from which a domestic animal descends.
Taming and breeding wild animals into domestic animals.
An area in the Middle East where agriculture arose.
A ball of hair or plant fibres in the stomach of an animal.

gewusst: Worldwide there are today about a billion domestic goats, all descended from the Bezoar goat.
Goat bones from excavations in Iran are among the oldest evidence of domestic animals.
In the past, bezoar stones were set in precious gold and silver mounts in Europe.

teile.einleitung: Biodiversity means the variety of life on Earth. It includes all animals, plants, fungi and tiny living things, but also their habitats and their genes. The greater this variety is, the more stable and resilient the ecosystems are.
wichtigste: Biodiversity means the variety of life, or biological diversity.
It covers the variety of species, of habitats and of genes.
Biodiversity makes ecosystems more stable and more resilient.
People depend on biodiversity, for example for food, clean water and pollination.
Around two million species have been scientifically described worldwide, and many more are unknown.
In Switzerland about a third of the species studied are endangered.
Loss of habitat, pollution, climate change and introduced species threaten the variety.

abschnitte.text: The word **biodiversity** is made up of “bios” for life and “diversitas” for variety. Experts distinguish three levels. **Species diversity** counts how many different species there are. Genetic diversity describes differences within a species, for example among apple varieties or breeds of cow. The variety of habitats includes forests, bogs, meadows, lakes and much more.

In a varied **ecosystem** many species take on similar tasks. If one species drops out, another can step in. That is why varied ecosystems are more stable and more resilient, for example against drought or pests. A mixed forest usually survives storms and beetle infestation better than a forest with only one species of tree. Just as a net with many knots holds better than one with few.

People benefit from biodiversity every day. Bees and other insects pollinate a large part of our fruit and vegetable plants. Soil organisms make the earth fertile, and forests and bogs store water and carbon. Many **medicines** originally come from plants, fungi or animals. Experts speak of **ecosystem services**.

Worldwide, far more species are dying out today than naturally. The biggest cause is the loss of **habitats**, for example through roads, settlements and intensive farming. In addition there are pesticides, over-fertilisation, overuse of the seas and climate change. Introduced species can also push out native ones. In Switzerland, for example, a large part of the bogs and river meadows has disappeared since 1900.

Thanks to the Alps, the Jura and the Central Plateau, Switzerland has many different habitats in a small area. Several tens of thousands of known species live here. According to the Red Lists, however, around a third of the species studied are endangered. In 2012 the Federal Council adopted a **Swiss Biodiversity Strategy**. In 2024 Switzerland voted on a biodiversity initiative, which was rejected.

Children and families too can promote diversity. A flower meadow instead of a closely cut lawn offers insects food. Piles of branches, piles of stones and hedges are hiding places for hedgehogs, lizards and birds. Anyone who buys seasonal and regional food and does without poison in the garden helps as well. Every year on 22 May is the International Day for Biological Diversity.

begriffe.erklaerung: A group of living things that can reproduce with each other.
A community of plants, animals and fungi together with their habitat.
A list of the endangered animal and plant species.
Things that nature does for people, such as clean water or pollination.

gewusst: A single spoonful of healthy garden soil contains more living things than there are people on Earth.
Most of the species on Earth are insects, and many of them have not yet been described by anyone.
In 1992 an international agreement to protect biodiversity was signed at the Earth Summit in Rio de Janeiro.

teile.einleitung: The brown trout is a typical fish of clear, cold streams and rivers and one of the best-known fish of Switzerland. You recognise it by its red and black spots. Because it needs clean, oxygen-rich water, it shows whether a body of water is healthy.
wichtigste: The brown trout lives in cold, flowing, clean water.
On its body it usually has red and black spots.
Most brown trout lay their eggs in autumn and winter.
Trout eggs need cool, oxygen-rich water.
The lake trout belongs to the same species, but lives in the lake.
In the wild a brown trout lives for about 5 to 10 years.
Dams are a problem because the fish can no longer reach their spawning grounds.

abschnitte.text: The brown trout, in Latin **Salmo trutta fario**, belongs, like the salmon, to the salmon family. Its back is usually brownish or olive green, and on its sides it has red and black spots that are often ringed with a pale border. In streams it usually grows to 20 to 40 centimetres long, in large rivers also more. On its back it has, like all salmonids, a small **adipose fin** without fin rays.

Brown trout like cold, flowing water with plenty of oxygen, as in mountain streams and the upper reaches of rivers. During the day, when it is very bright, it often hides in the shade under stones, roots or overhanging banks. It swims fastest with powerful movements of its tail. In polluted or too warm water, trout get into trouble and can die, which is why they count as an **indicator species** for healthy waters.

Brown trout eat insect larvae, freshwater shrimps, worms and insects that fall into the water. Large animals also hunt small fish. Young trout are often hunted by **grey herons** and the kingfisher. Goosanders, cormorants and otters also eat trout.

Most brown trout spawn in autumn and winter. The female beats a pit into the gravel with her tail, a so-called **redd**, and lays the eggs there. The eggs need cool, oxygen-rich water that flows through the gravel. After a few weeks the **alevins** hatch, which at first feed on their yolk sac on the belly.

The brown trout occurs in Switzerland in almost all streams from the Central Plateau up into the Alps. The **lake trout** belongs to the same species, but grows up in the lake and migrates into the inflowing streams to spawn. In recent decades the populations have fallen sharply in many places. The reasons are warmer water, diseases, river engineering and power stations that block the migration to the spawning grounds.

begriffe.erklaerung: Laying eggs and fertilising them, in fish and amphibians.
A store of nutrients on the belly of a newly hatched fish larva.
An animal or plant whose presence shows the condition of the environment.
A form of the trout that lives in the lake and migrates into rivers to spawn.

gewusst: Lake trout can grow to more than a metre long, much bigger than brown trout in a stream.
Depending on the water, the same species of trout can be very differently coloured, almost silvery or very dark.

teile.einleitung: The ampullae of Lorenzini are tiny sense organs on the snouts of sharks and rays. With them the animals can sense very weak electrical signals sent out by other living things. This “sixth sense” helps sharks to find even prey that is hidden in the sand.
wichtigste: The ampullae of Lorenzini are sense organs for electric fields.
They sit mainly on the snout and head of sharks and rays.
You can see them as small pores in the skin.
The pores lead to canals filled with a gel.
Every living thing produces weak electrical signals, for example with its heartbeat and muscle movements.
They are named after the Italian Stefano Lorenzini, who described them in 1678.
Sharks are among the animals with the finest electrical sense.

abschnitte.text: The **ampullae of Lorenzini** are small sense organs in the skin of sharks, rays and chimaeras. From the outside you can only see tiny holes, the **pores**, often scattered like freckles over the snout. Each pore leads into a canal filled with a clear gel. At the end of the canal there is a small bulb, the ampulla, with sensory cells. A shark can have hundreds to thousands of these ampullae.

abschnitte.titel: How does the electrical sense work?
abschnitte.text: All animals produce weak electrical voltages, for example with every heartbeat, with muscle movements and when breathing. In salty seawater these **electric fields** spread out a little. The gel in the canals carries the voltage very well to the sensory cells. These report to the brain where the source is. In this way the shark can sense voltages that are many thousands of times weaker than those of a small battery.

With the **electrical sense**, sharks and rays find prey over the last few centimetres, even when they cannot see anything. A flatfish buried in the sand gives itself away by the movements of its gills. **Hammerhead sharks** have their ampullae spread across their whole broad head and use them to sweep the seabed like a metal detector. Just before biting, many sharks close their eyes or protect them, and then only the electrical sense helps them. Sharks may also use these organs to find their way by the Earth's magnetic field.

The Italian doctor **Stefano Lorenzini** described the organs in 1678 in an electric ray. But he did not know what they were for. For a long time researchers thought they measured pressure or temperature. Only around 1960 did scientists find out that they are sense organs for electric fields. Since then the electrical sense has also been discovered in other animals.

Some other animals also sense electric fields, such as sturgeons, catfish and many lungfish. The **platypus** in Australia uses electroreceptors in its bill to find worms and crustaceans in the mud. Even bumblebees can detect electric charges on flowers. Researchers use this knowledge to develop electric **shark deterrents** for surfers and divers. These send out strong electrical signals that disturb the sharks' electrical sense.

begriffe.erklaerung: A part of the body with which a living thing notices something in its surroundings, for example an eye or an ear.
An invisible region around an electrical voltage that can be measured.
A tiny opening in the skin.

teile.einleitung: The blue-ringed octopus is a small octopus from the Pacific and the Indian Ocean. It is hardly bigger than a golf ball, but its poison is among the strongest in the animal kingdom. When it feels threatened, blue rings light up on its skin.
wichtigste: The blue-ringed octopus is known for its very strong poison.
It is a small octopus, usually only about 10 to 20 centimetres including the arms.
When in danger, blue rings light up on its skin.
It lives in warm coastal waters from Japan to Australia.
Its poison is called tetrodotoxin, and there is no antidote.
It eats mainly small crustaceans and crabs.

abschnitte.text: Blue-ringed octopuses are small, and their body is only about as big as a golf ball. Together with the eight arms they usually measure 10 to 20 centimetres. Normally they are an inconspicuous yellowish or brown colour. When they feel threatened, bright **blue rings** appear on the skin. This warning colour tells enemies: careful, I am poisonous.

Blue-ringed octopuses live in warm, shallow coastal waters of the **Pacific** and the Indian Ocean. They are found from Japan across South-East Asia to Australia. They like to hide in rock crevices, shells and among corals. They are often in tide pools, where they are easily overlooked.

The poison of the blue-ringed octopus is called **tetrodotoxin**. It is made by bacteria in its salivary glands. The poison paralyses the muscles, including the breathing muscles. Even a small, often painless bite can be life-threatening for a person. There is no **antidote**, but those affected can be saved by artificial respiration until the poison is broken down.

Blue-ringed octopuses hunt mainly **crabs** and small crustaceans as well as small fish. They bite their prey or release poison into the water to paralyse it. Like other octopuses they can change colour quickly. Towards people they are rather shy and bite only if they are picked up or crowded.

The female lays eggs only once in her life, usually about 50 to 100. She carries the eggs under her arms and guards them until the young hatch. During this time she hardly eats and dies shortly afterwards. Blue-ringed octopuses live only about one to two years.

begriffe.erklaerung: A strong nerve poison that paralyses muscles.

gewusst: A blue-ringed octopus is so small that it fits in a child's hand, and is still one of the most poisonous sea creatures.
The same poison as in the blue-ringed octopus is also found in the pufferfish.
The blue rings can light up in a fraction of a second.

teile.einleitung: The Big Five are five large wild animals of Africa: lion, leopard, rhinoceros, elephant and Cape buffalo. The term comes from big-game hunters, for whom these animals counted as especially dangerous. Today tourists on safari want to see all five with their cameras.
wichtigste: The Big Five include the lion, leopard, rhinoceros, elephant and Cape buffalo.
The name comes from hunters' language and described the animals most dangerous to hunt on foot.
Today the Big Five stand for photo safaris instead of hunting.
As a Big Five animal the Cape buffalo attracts many visitors and is so important for conservation and tourism.
Well-known places for Big Five safaris are Kruger National Park, the Serengeti and the Masai Mara.
Rhinoceroses and elephants are severely threatened by poaching.
The money from tourism helps to pay for protected areas and rangers.

abschnitte.text: The term **Big Five** is a name in English, and in German it means “the great five”. It arose over a hundred years ago among big-game hunters in Africa. What was meant were the five animals that were the most difficult and dangerous to hunt on foot. So it was not about the biggest animals, otherwise the giraffe and the hippopotamus would belong too. Today mainly safari organisers use the term.

The **African elephant** is the largest land animal on Earth. The lion is the only big cat that lives in prides. The **leopard** is a shy loner that often drags its prey up into trees and is the hardest to spot. The rhinoceros here means the white rhinoceros and the black rhinoceros. The **Cape buffalo** lives in large herds and is regarded as unpredictable when it is wounded or pressed.

You can watch all five animals in some protected areas in eastern and southern Africa. Well known are **Kruger National Park** in South Africa, the Serengeti and the Ngorongoro Crater in Tanzania and the Masai Mara in Kenya. There are also such parks in Botswana, Zambia and Zimbabwe. In the early morning and in the evening the animals are most active.

Some Big Five animals are severely endangered. Rhinoceroses are poached for their horn, elephants for their ivory. The **black rhinoceros** is critically endangered. Lions too have lost a great deal of habitat in recent decades. Rangers, tracker dogs and strict laws are meant to protect the animals.

Many people travel to Africa to see the Big Five. With the money from entrance fees and accommodation, **national parks** and rangers are paid for. The people in the villages around them also earn money from it. In this way it is worthwhile for everyone to protect the animals instead of hunting them. The South African rand banknotes have shown the Big Five since 2012.

gewusst: There are also the “Little Five” with animals such as the antlion, the elephant shrew and the rhinoceros beetle.
